NASHR:v2p138/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p138/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p138/r5.claim: Ibn Ghalbūn, Sibt al-Khayyāṭ, and Ibn Sawwār explicitly document بالواد المقدس at both occurrences; Abū al-ʿAlāʾ cites it by analogy.
NASHR:v2p138/r5.anchor: ونص على بالواد المقدس في الموضعين أبو الحسن بن غلبون وأبو محمد سبط الخياط

NASHR:v2p138/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p138/r11.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p138/r11.claim: Al-Kisāʾī agrees on وادي النمل by the majority route; some transmitters add both بالواد المقدس sites and الواد الأيمن, while many Iraqi authorities report deletion at all four.
NASHR:v2p138/r11.anchor: ووافقه على وادي النمل الكسائي فيما رواه الجمهور عنه

QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.claim: When Moses connects with the fire, he is called beyond fiery curtains of majesty; “I am your Lord” is God's manifestation veiled in a fiery form.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r6.anchor: أي: اتصل بها { نودي } من وراء

QASHANI:20:6-12/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r7.claim: The sandals signify self and body or the two worlds; casting them off means cutting attachments and effacing attributes and acts to connect with the sacred realm.

QASHANI:20:6-12/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:6-12/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:6-12/r8.claim: They are called sandals rather than clothes because connection requires leaving their coverings behind; Moses must detach completely.
QASHANI:20:6-12/r8.anchor: وإنما سماهما نعلين ولم يسمهما ثوبين لأنه لو لم يتجرد عن ملابسهما

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r12.claim: One explanation says sandals are removed because no one treads with shoes on a king’s court.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r12.anchor: فإن بساط حضرة الملوك لا يوطأ بنعل

QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r13.claim: The inward meaning of removing both sandals is to empty the heart of concerns about both worlds and devote oneself wholly to God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p253/r13.anchor: تفريغ القلب من حديث الدارين ، والتجرد للحق بنعت الانفراد

FARRA:v2p175/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r4.claim: A report says Moses was told to remove sandals made from the hide of a dead donkey.
FARRA:v2p175/r4.anchor: ذكر أنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت فأمر بخلعهما

FARRA:v2p175/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r5.claim: طوى with kasra is normally declined; as a place-name it may be indeclinable, like Ḥunayn when understood as a town.

FARRA:v2p175/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r6.claim: A poet leaves حنين and جبل حراء uninflected when treating each as a place-name; with ḍamma, طوى is usually declined but can also be indeclinable.
FARRA:v2p175/r6.anchor: وقال الشاعر في ترك إجرائه: نصروا نبيهم

NAHHAS:v3p33/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r8.speaker: أهل المدينة وأهل البصرة
NAHHAS:v3p33/r8.claim: The Medinans and Basrans read طوى without tanwīn; the Kufans add tanwīn.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r8.anchor: بغير تنوين وقرأ أهل الكوفة ( طوى ) بالتنوين

NAHHAS:v3p33/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r9.claim: Al-Nahhas prefers no tanwīn because طوى is a shifted proper name like عمر, or a feminine place name.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر الوجه ترك التنوين لأنه مثل عمر معدول وهو معرفة

NAHHAS:v3p33/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p33/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq treats the tanwīn form as an unshifted place name like حطم or صرد; طوى meaning “folded twice” takes no tanwīn and is linked to a hadith against double collection.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r10.anchor: ومن نون فزعم أبو إسحاق أنه يقدره اسما للمكان غير معدول مثل حطم وصرد

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r5.claim: They read Ṭuwā with ḍamma and no tanwīn; another group uses ḍamma with tanwīn, while a reading reported from Abū ʿAmr has kasra without declension, treating it as a place-name.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r5.anchor: في طوى ثلاث قراءات: الأولى: بضم الطاء غير منون

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r6.claim: No tanwīn may reflect a place-name or a form altered from Ṭāwin; tanwīn reflects masculine treatment and lightening, and readers differ between tafkhīm and imāla because of the yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r6.anchor: أما ترك الإجراء لأنه اسم البقعة أو هو معدول من طاو

MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:9-12/r2.claim: At the valley Tuwa, God calls Moses and orders him to remove sandals made from the skin of an unritually dead donkey; Tuwa is the valley’s name and means the purified valley.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r1.claim: The verse about taking one's adornment at every mosque can support the view that prayer in clean sandals is preferable.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī says he wished a needy person would come and take the sandals of those who remove them.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the instruction to remove one's sandals between one's feet during prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r3.anchor: إذا صلى أحدكم فليخلع نعليه بين رجليه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra advises al-Maqburī to place removed sandals between the feet so they do not inconvenience another Muslim.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's placing sandals to his left applies when leading or praying alone; a follower should avoid harming the person on the left, and should place them ahead rather than between the feet.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r5.anchor: فإن كنت إماما أو وحدك فافعل ذلك إن أحببت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r6.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r6.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim calls placing sandals between one's feet an innovation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r6.anchor: وضع الرجل نعليه بين قدميه بدعة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r7.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأكثر العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r7.claim: Agreed major impurities such as blood, human excrement, and urine require washing with water to purify sandals or footwear.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r8.claim: Maliki jurists differ whether rubbing earth purifies sandals or leather socks from disputed animal urine and wet dung.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r8.anchor: فهل يطهرها المسح بالتراب من النعل والخف أو لا؟ قولان عندنا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r9.speaker: الأوزاعي وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r9.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and Abū Thawr allow earth-rubbing without qualification for such animal impurities.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r9.anchor: وأطلق الإجزاء بمسح ذلك بالتراب من غير تفصيل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says dried filth is removed by scraping and rubbing, while wet filth, including urine, requires washing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: يزيله إذا يبس الحك والفرك، ولا يزيل رطبه إلا الغسل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r11.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r11.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that none of those impurities is purified except with water.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r11.anchor: لا يطهر شيئا من ذلك كله إلا الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r12.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the view that rubbing purifies filth from leather socks and sandals, based on the report of Abū Saʿīd.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:9-16#2/r12.anchor: والصحيح قول من قال: إن المسح يطهره من الخف والنعل لحديث أبي سعيد

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r7.speaker: يروى
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r7.claim: One report says Moses had to remove sandals made from the hide of a dead donkey.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r7.anchor: روي أنه أمر بخلعهما لأنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r8.speaker: يروى
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r8.claim: Another report says the sandals were removed so Moses could tread the holy valley with his feet; a further report says it had been sanctified twice.
ZAJJAJ:v3p350#2/r8.anchor:
وروي أنه أمر
بخلعهما ليطأ بقدميه الوادي المقدس، وروي أنه قدس مرتين.

TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r1.speaker: جعفر الصادق
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r1.claim: Al-Faqih reports al-Sadiq explaining that Moses' sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; al-Qummi and Sunni transmitters also report this, while the context points to reverence for the place.
TABATABAI:20:9-48#2/r1.anchor: وفي الفقيه سئل الصادق عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل

TABRISI:20:9-16/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-16/r8.claim: Ṭuwā may be declinable as the masculine name of a valley, or an adjective meaning blessed twice, like thunā and suwā; it may also take either ḍamma or kasra.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r8.anchor: أن يجعله اسم الوادي فيصرفه لأنه سمي مذكرا بمذكر

TABRISI:20:9-16/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-16/r9.claim: If uninflected, Ṭuwā may be a place or land name, or a form made indeclinable by alteration like ʿUmar; alteration can be posited even when its original form is unattested.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r9.anchor: أن يكون اسما لبقعة أو أرض فهو مذكر فيكون بمنزلة امرأة سميتها بحجر

THALABI:v6p239#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p239#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says Tuwa is a circular, deep valley; other interpretations relate the name to traversing the valley, night, or blessing folded into it.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: مستدير عميق مثل الطوى في استدارته

THALABI:v6p239#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p239#2/r7.claim: Ikrima reads طوى with kasra on the ṭāʾ; the text says the form has two dialectal readings.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: طوى بكسر الطاء وهما لغتان

THALABI:v6p239#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p239#2/r8.claim: Kufan and Syrian readers use tanwin and genitive inflection; others omit tanwin because the word is a diptote derived from طاو or مطوي.
THALABI:v6p239#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة والشام: طوى بالتنوين وإلا جرا لتذكيره وتحقيقه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r6.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r6.claim: Some exegetes discuss the material of Moses’s shoes, while the more common interpretation says he was to touch the sacred place directly and receive its blessing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r6.anchor: daha çok ayaklarının o kutsal mekâna doğrudan temas etmesinin ve bereketinden nasiplenmesinin istendiği yorumu tercih edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r7.claim: The author suggests removing the shoes prepared Moses spiritually for revelation and called him to show special respect, an interpretation close to Ibn ʿAtiyya’s.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r7.anchor: İbn Atıyye de buna yakın bir yorum yapmaktadır (IV, 39)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r8.speaker: Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r8.claim: Asad renders Ṭuwā as “twice blessed,” based on the reading that relates it to a word meaning “twice.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r8.anchor: “tuvâ” (diğer okunuşuyla “tıvâ”) kelimesiyle ilgili olarak şu açıklamayı yapmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r9.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r9.claim: Zamakhshari first mentions Ṭuwā as a place name, then reports that it may mean “twice,” including either being blessed twice or being addressed twice; the author corrects Asad’s description of Zamakhshari.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r9.anchor: Zemahşerî önce bu kelimenin yer adı olmasına ilişkin yoruma temas etmekte, daha sonra “İki defa anlamına geldiği de söylenmiştir” şeklinde kendi yorum ve tercihi olmaksızın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r10.claim: Exegetes generally transmit both interpretations of Ṭuwā, whether or not they state a preference: a valley’s name or the word “twice.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:9/r10.anchor: genellikle müfessirler –tercih belirterek veya belirtmeden– her iki yorumu (vadi ismi olduğunu ve iki kere mânasına geldiğini) nakletmektedirler

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r9.claim: Removing shoes expresses cleanliness, decency, and humility in God’s presence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r9.anchor: This is not only among the etiquette of cleanliness but also a norm of decency and humility.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r10.claim: Removing shoes in mosques is mandatory for the same reasons of cleanliness and humility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r10.anchor: taking off shoes in the mosques has been made mandatory precisely for this reason.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r11.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r11.claim: Some hold that clean shoes may be worn in a mosque.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r11.anchor: Some people ar e of the opinion that if the shoes are clean

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r12.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r12.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r12.claim: Islahi rejects that view because clean shoes still violate the humility and decorum required in a mosque.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r12.anchor: this is not correct because this would be against decency and humility

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r13.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r13.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r13.claim: Ṭuwā is a broad plain at Sinai’s base and is called sacred because of its special association with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r13.anchor: This is a vast flat land situated at the base of mount Sinai.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r14.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r14.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r14.claim: All parts of the earth were created by God and have no superiority over one another in themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p17/r14.anchor: All parts of the earth have been created by God and do not have any superiority over one another

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r1.claim: A place becomes sacred through its special association with God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r1.anchor: except if some part has some special association with God.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r3.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، عاصم، نافع، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r3.claim: They differ in إني أنا: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open the hamza and yāʾ; the other listed readers use kasra on the hamza, with Nafi alone opening the yāʾ and the rest quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ﴿ إني أنا ﴾ بفتح الألف والياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r4.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، عاصم، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read طوى without declension and with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai decline it. Abu Zayd glosses it as a land.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ﴿ طوى وأنا ﴾ غير مجراة والطاء مضمومة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r6.claim: Khulʿ and naʿl mean removing sandals; naʿl may be foot protection made of leather, iron, or wood, and Ṭuwā is a place-name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p307/r6.anchor: الخلع والنعل معروفان وهو إزالتها من الرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r4.claim: The order to remove sandals reflects the gravity of the moment and humility before God, as before kings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن أمره تعالى إياه بخلع النعلين لعظم الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r5.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل والكلبي والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r5.claim: They say the sandals were untanned hide of a dead donkey and removed for impurity; a Tirmidhī report is called gharīb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r5.anchor: جلد حمار ميت غير مدبوغ قول عكرمة وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r6.claim: Another view says the sandals were ritually slaughtered cowhide, removed so Moses’s feet could receive the sacred valley’s blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p315/r6.anchor: وقيل: كانتا من جلد بقرة ذكي لكن أمر بخلعهما لبيان بركة الوادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r1.claim: A report says God created Moses’s sandals and he cast them beyond the valley.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r1.anchor: وروي أنه خلق نعليه وألقاهما من وراء الوادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r2.claim: Muqaddas means purified; Ṭuwā is a proper place name in apposition or explanatory apposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r2.anchor: والمقدس المطهر وطوى اسم علم عليه فيكون بدلا أو عطف بيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r3.speaker: الحسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو السمال وابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r3.claim: These readers use kasra and tanwīn; other readers use ḍamma with or without tanwīn, and some use kasra without tanwīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو السمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r4.claim: Tanwīn indicates a place; uninflected readings may treat Ṭuwā as shifted, foreign, or a feminine place-name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r4.anchor: فمن نون فعلى تأويل المكان، ومن لم ينون وضم الطاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r5.speaker: الحسن وقطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan treats Ṭuwā as a verbal noun for blessing and sanctifying twice; Quṭrub says it means an hour of night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: طوى بكسر الطاء والتنوين مصدر ثنيت فيه البركة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Hafs read the clause with the preposition omitted and a fatḥa; other readers understand an implied verb of saying.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r5.anchor: مسقطا الجار في قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو وأبي حفص بالفتح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r6.claim: Moses is told to remove his sandals as courtly etiquette, to receive their blessing, and to settle without turning back toward family; dream interpreters take footwear to signify a child.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r6.anchor: كما يفعل بحضرات الملوك أدبا , ولتنالك بركتها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r7.claim: The sacred valley is purified of what is unfit for a king's court; the wording also indicates that God is not contained by place or time.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r7.anchor: أي المطهر عن كل ما لا يليق بأفنية الملوك

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.claim: It is said that God called to Moses from a tree in the valley.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r1.anchor: It is said that in the valley God called to Moses from a tree (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r2.speaker: JJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r2.claim: The tree is identified as a kind of lycium or boxthorn (ʿawsaj) plant.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r2.anchor: that was a kind of lycium or boxthorn (ʿawsaj

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.claim: One interpretation takes the referent to be the tree from which God called Moses.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r3.anchor: It thus refers to the tree (JJ) or, alternately,

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ, Bg, R
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies it with the fire Moses saw, which consumed the tree.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r4.anchor: to the fire that Moses perceived (see v. 10; IK, R, Ṭ) and which consumed the tree (Bg, R)

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r5.claim: One report says Moses was told to remove his sandals because they were made from the skin of a dead donkey.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r5.anchor: either because they were made of the skin of a dead donkey (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r6.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r6.claim: Removing the sandals is explained as reverence for sacred space, as people remove shoes before entering the Kaʿbah sanctuary or any mosque.

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r7.speaker: al-Ghazzālī
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r7.claim: Al-Ghazzālī reads the command as casting aside attachment to both this world and the next, turning wholly toward God.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r7.anchor: al-Ghazzālīsuggests that in being asked to remove his sandals Moses was being instructed to cast aside this world and the next world

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r8.speaker: My, Qu
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r8.claim: Sufis take the phrase to mean that the heart should be free of attachment to both worlds and devoted solely to God.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r8.anchor: for Sufis the verse means that one’s heart should be free of any attachment to the things to be found in this world

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r9.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah glosses the phrase as leaving the two realms of existence to witness the Presence of the Existentiator.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r9.anchor: As Ibn ʿAjībah explains it, the phrase means,

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r10.claim: The sandals became a recurrent Sufi image and symbol in poetry and inspired literary works, including Ibn Qasī’s book Taking Off the Sandals.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r10.anchor: has inspired a number of artful literary works in Islamic civilization, such as the book Taking Off the Sandals

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r11.claim: A famous poem attributed to Ibn ʿArabī explains the Divine intent as relinquishing both worlds and removing the veils between.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r11.anchor: In a famous poem attributed to Ibn ʿArabī, the Divine intent behind the imagery is explained:

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r12.claim: Ṭuwā derives from a root meaning “to fold up” or “to become enwrapped.”
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r12.anchor: the name of the holy valley in which Moses encounters God is Ṭuwā, which comes from a root that means “to fold up”

STUDYQURAN:20:11/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r13.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r13.claim: The valley symbolizes the inner holy sanctuary and Ocean of Divine Presence, where existence is folded up and Moses’ soul is enwrapped in Divine Reality.
STUDYQURAN:20:11/r13.anchor: the inner, holy sanctuary that symbolizes the Ocean of the Divine Presence above all states of existence (Aj)

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r4.claim: One explanation is that the sandals were made from carrion donkey hide, which God did not want brought onto the sacred valley; Moses was to touch its blessing.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r4.anchor: فقال بعضهم: أمره بذلك، لأنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت، فكره أن يطأ بهما الوادي المقدس

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r5.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r5.claim: Kaʿb says the sandals were carrion donkey hide, and God wanted Moses to touch the sacred place.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r5.anchor: عن كعب، أنه رآهم يخلعون نعالهم {اخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} فقال: كانت من جلد حمار ميت، فأراد الله أن يمسه القدس

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r6.claim: Ikrima reports that Moses’ sandals were made of carrion donkey hide.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله {فاخلع نعليك} [طه: 12] قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r7.claim: Qatada reports that the sandals were donkey hide and Moses removed them before approaching.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: حدثنا أن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار، فخلعهما ثم أتاه

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r8.claim: Ali likewise says the sandals were donkey hide; the segment adds that Qatada held the same view.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r8.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، {فاخلع نعليك} [طه: 12] قال: كانتا من جلد حمار، فقيل له اخلعهما قال: وقال قتادة مثل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p22/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r9.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r9.claim: Another view says the sandals were cowhide; God wanted Moses’ bare feet to receive the earth’s blessing.
TAB-FULL:v16p22/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: كانتا من جلد بقر، ولكن الله أراد أن يطأ موسى الأرض بقدميه، ليصل إليه بركتها

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the sandals were cowhide and Moses was to touch the earth’s blessing directly; the valley had been sanctified twice.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: كانتا يعني نعلي موسى من بقر، ولكن إنما أراد الله أن يباشر بقدميه بركة الأرض، وكان قد قدس مرتين

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r2.claim: Mujahid rejects the claim that the sandals were carrion hide: Moses was commanded to touch the earth’s blessing with his feet.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r2.anchor: وقيل لمجاهد: زعموا أن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار أو ميتة، قال: لا، ولكنه أمر أن يباشر بقدميه بركة الأرض

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r3.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Najih glosses the command as bringing Moses’ feet into contact with the valley’s blessing.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r3.anchor: سمعت ابن أبي نجيح، يقول في قوله: {فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: يقول: أفض بقدميك إلى بركة الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that Moses remove the sandals to touch the blessed valley directly: the verse links the command to the valley’s sanctity, while neither the Qur’an nor an authoritative report establishes impurity or donkey hide.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: أمره الله تعالى ذكره بخلع نعليه ليباشر بقدميه بركة الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r5.speaker: نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet describes Moses in wool garments and sandals of untanned donkey hide; al-Tabari says its chain needs scrutiny and would not rely on it without that problem.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r5.anchor: عن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: " يوم كلم الله موسى، كانت عليه جبة صوف

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r6.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r6.claim: Some Medinan and Basran readers open the hamza of أني, making it a clause governed by نودي and meaning that this saying was called out.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r6.anchor: فقرأ ذلك بعض قراء المدينة والبصرة

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r7.speaker: بعض عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r7.claim: Other leading Medinan and Kufan readers use kasra in إني, treating it as the start of a new clause: Moses was told, ‘I am your Lord.’
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r7.anchor: وقرأه بعض عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة بالكسر

TAB-FULL:v16p24/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r8.claim: Al-Tabari prefers kasra because يا موسى intervenes between نودي and إني; if the verb governed the clause, the construction would be نودي أن يا موسى إني.
TAB-FULL:v16p24/r8.anchor: والكسر أولى القراءتين عندنا بالصواب، وذلك أن النداء قد حال بينه وبين العمل

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r1.claim: Al-Tabari calls the valley purified and blessed; Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd also describe it as blessed.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس} يقول: المبارك

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r2.claim: Mujahid says the valley was sanctified and blessed twice.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد، قوله {إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: قدس بورك مرتين

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r3.claim: One interpretation takes طوى as a verbal noun meaning that Moses traversed the sacred valley.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: معناه: إنك بالوادي المقدس طويته، فعلى هذا القول من قولهم طوى مصدر خرج من غير لفظه

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses crossed the sacred land at night and went up to the valley’s higher part.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} يعني الأرض المقدسة، وذلك أنه مر بواديها ليلا فطواه

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes طوى to mean twice: God called Moses twice, in two calls.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: مرتين، وقال: ناداه ربه مرتين

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r6.speaker: عدي بن زيد العبادي
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r6.claim: Al-Tabari cites Adi ibn Zayd’s verse as evidence for طوى meaning repeated or twice.

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r7.claim: Others transmit the poetic word as ثنى, meaning again and again, and say ثنى and طوى are synonymous.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r7.anchor: وروى ذلك آخرون: علي ثنى: أي مرة بعد أخرى، وقالوا: طوى وثنى بمعنى واحد

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r8.claim: Qatada says the valley was sanctified twice and was named Ṭuwā.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، {فاخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} كنا نحدث أنه واد قدس مرتين، وأن اسمه طوى

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r9.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the valley had been sanctified twice.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r9.anchor: قال الحسن: كان قد قدس مرتين

TAB-FULL:v16p27/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r10.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r10.claim: Another view treats Ṭuwā as the name of the valley.
TAB-FULL:v16p27/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل طوى: اسم الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ṭuwā is the name of the valley.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {طوى} [طه: 12] اسم للوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r2.claim: Mujahid also identifies Ṭuwā as the valley’s name.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: طوى: قال: اسم الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ṭuwā is the valley where Moses stood and received what God gave him, near the mountain.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r3.anchor: قال: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {بالواد المقدس طوى}

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r4.claim: Another interpretation reads the phrase as God telling Moses to tread the valley barefoot.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل هو أمر من الله لموسى أن يطأ الوادي بقدميه

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses طوى as an instruction to tread the valley.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله تبارك وتعالى: {اخلع نعليك إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: طأ الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r6.claim: Ikrima likewise interprets طوى as ‘tread the valley.’
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {طوى} [طه: 12] قال: طأ الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Moses was to tread barefoot, as one enters the Kaaba barefoot, to receive the valley’s blessing.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قول الله {طوى} [طه: 12] قال: طأ الأرض حافيا، كما تدخل الكعبة حافيا، يقول: من بركة الوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses Ṭuwā as treading the earth barefoot.

TAB-FULL:v16p29/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r9.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r9.claim: Some Medinan readers pronounce Ṭuwā with ḍamma and no tanwin, treating it as the name of the land; the uninflected place name Ḥunayn is their analogy.
TAB-FULL:v16p29/r9.anchor: فلم يجر حنين، لأنه جعله اسما للبلدة لا للوادي

TAB-FULL:v16p30/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r1.claim: The reading without tanwin also leaves Ḥirāʾ uninflected because it is treated as a place name, supporting the same analysis of Ṭuwā.
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r1.anchor: ألسنا أكرم الثقلين رحلا … وأعظمهم ببطن حراء نارا فلم يجر حراء، وهو جبل، لأنه جعله اسما للبلدة

TAB-FULL:v16p30/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r2.speaker: عامة قراء أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r2.claim: Most Kufan readers pronounce Ṭuwā with ḍamma and tanwin.
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل الكوفة: {طوى} [طه: 12] بضم الطاء والتنوين

TAB-FULL:v16p30/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the reading with tanwin: it fits whether Ṭuwā is a verbal noun or, as he judges, a masculine valley name; as a name it is genitive in apposition to الوادي.
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأه بضم الطاء والتنوين، لأنه إن يكن اسما للوادي فحظه التنوين

TAB-FULL:v16p30/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r4.claim: If Ṭuwā is the valley’s name, al-Tabari places it in the genitive as an appositive to الوادي.
TAB-FULL:v16p30/r4.anchor: وهو عندي اسم الوادي. وإذ كان ذلك كذلك، فهو في موضع خفض ردا على الوادي

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r1.claim: Places and times such as the Kaaba, mosques, shrines, feasts, and blessed days gain holiness through association with a noble event or prescribed worship; place and time have no inherent ranking.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r1.anchor: فإنما ذلك قدس وشرف اكتسبته بالانتساب إلى واقعة شريفة وقعت فيها أو نسك وعبادة مقدسة شرعت فيها

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.claim: Moses knew with certainty that his Lord spoke to him: in revelation the addressee apprehends no other speaker, consistent with the Quran's account of divine communication.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r2.anchor: فهم من ذلك فهم يقين أن الذي يكلمه هو ربه والكلام كلامه وذلك أنه كان وحيا منه تعالى

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.claim: A prophet's first reception of prophecy or mission is immediate and certain; needing rational proof would make it acquired inference rather than reception from the unseen.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r3.anchor: ولو افتقر إلى شيء من ذلك كان اكتسابا بواسطة القوة النظرية لا تلقيا من الغيب من غير توسط واسطة

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r5.claim: Saying 'I am your Lord' rather than 'I am Allah' or 'Lord of the worlds' marks a moment of direct audience and God's special attention to Moses.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r5.anchor: تنبيه لموسى على أن الموقف موقف الحضور ومقام المشافهة وقد خلى به وخصه من نفسه بمزيد العناية

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.claim: The first divine address clears the setting of others for revelation; the later 'I am Allah' is the revealed message itself, so it is not redundant.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r6.anchor: لأن الأول تخلية للمقام من الأغيار

TABRISI:20:12-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r1.claim: The wording is linked to God's call to Moses from the tree in the account at 28:30.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r2.claim: The command to cast down the staff is linked to the sign in 7:117.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:12-14/r3.claim: One account says Moses saw a green tree blazing with white fire, heard the angels glorifying God, and saw a great light; neither the greenery quenched the fire nor the fire burned it. He was bewildered, recognized a supernatural sign, received calm, and was called.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r3.anchor: شجرة خضراء من أسفلها إلى أعلاها تتوقد فيها نار بيضاء

TABRISI:20:12-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r4.claim: The repeated pronoun strengthens the evidence, removes doubt, and establishes certain knowledge.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r4.anchor: وإنما كرر الكناية لتأكيد الدلالة وإزالة الشبهة وتحقيق المعرفة

TABRISI:20:12-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r5.claim: The command means to remove the two sandals.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r6.speaker: كعب وعكرمة والصادق
TABRISI:20:12-14/r6.claim: One explanation says the sandals were made of the hide of a dead donkey; this is attributed to Ka'b and Ikrima and also transmitted from al-Sadiq.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r6.anchor: أنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت عن كعب وعكرمة

TABRISI:20:12-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وابن جريج
TABRISI:20:12-14/r7.claim: Another explanation says the sandals were from a properly slaughtered cow; Moses was told to remove them so his feet could touch the blessed valley's ground.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r7.anchor: كانتا من جلد بقرة ذكية ولكنه أمر بخلعهما ليباشر بقدميه الأرض

TABRISI:20:12-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r8.speaker: الأصم
TABRISI:20:12-14/r8.claim: Bare feet signify humility; the early generations therefore performed circumambulation barefoot.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r8.anchor: أن الحفاء من علامة التواضع ولذلك كانت السلف تطوف حفاة عن الأصم

TABRISI:20:12-14/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:12-14/r9.claim: Moses had worn sandals to avoid impurity and insects; God reassured him that he was safe and the place was pure.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r9.anchor: اتقاء من الأنجاس وخوفا من الحشرات

TABRISI:20:12-14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:12-14/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the sacred valley as blessed, with abundant provision and fertility.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r10.anchor: المبارك عن ابن عباس بورك فيه بسعة الرزق والخصب

TABRISI:20:12-14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:12-14/r11.claim: Another gloss takes المقدس to mean purified.

TABRISI:20:12-14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجبائي
TABRISI:20:12-14/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Jubba'i take طوى as the valley's proper name.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r12.anchor: هو اسم الوادي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والجبائي

TABRISI:20:12-14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:20:12-14/r13.claim: Hasan says the valley was named طوى because it was sanctified twice, as if folded twice in blessing.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r13.anchor: سمي به لأن الوادي قدس مرتين فكأنه طوي بالبركة مرتين عن الحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r2.speaker: نوف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r2.claim: Nawf says Moses asked who was calling him, and the answer was, “I am your Lord Most High.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r2.anchor: قال نوف (¬1): (فلما سمع النداء قال: من أنت الذي تناديني وتدعوني؟ قال: أنا ربك الأعلى فذلك قوله: {إني أنا ربك}) (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r3.speaker: القراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r3.claim: A variant reading has fatḥa on the initial hamza: annī rather than innī.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says fatḥa makes the phrase the content of “he was called” with an accusative position; kasra treats it as direct speech after “he was called.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: (من فتح كان المعنى نودي أني أنا ربك. وموضع أن نصب، ومن كسر فالمعنى:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r5.claim: Abu Ali explains kasra as quoted speech—“he was called, and it was said: O Moses, I am your Lord”—while fatḥa gives the content of the call, since nādā can take a prepositional complement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r5.anchor: وشرحه أبو علي فقال: (من كسر فلأن هذا الكلام حكاية، كأنه نودي فقيل: يا موسى إني أنا ربك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r6.claim: A cited Arabic verse illustrates the construction in which nādā is followed by the particle ann.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p365#2/r6.anchor: ناديت باسم ربيعة بن مكدم ... أن المنوه باسمه الموثوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r1.claim: Khalaʿ means to remove; a naʿl is a covering for the feet against the ground, with related forms for wearing sandals.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Masud, traced to the Prophet, says Moses’ sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; Ali, Sufyan, Kaʿb, and most others share this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r2.anchor: فروى ابن مسعود عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في هذه الآية قال: "كانتا من جلد حمار ميت" (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the command meant that Moses should not enter the valley while wearing the sandals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي: (كانت نعلا، فقيل] (¬5) له: لا تدخل الوادي وهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses was to touch the ground with his feet because he was in a sacred valley.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: (يريد: باشر الأرض بقدميك فإنك بواد مقدس) (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r5.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد وابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and others say the sandals were of ritually slaughtered cowhide; Moses was to touch the sacred soil and receive its blessing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: (كانتا من جلد بقرة ذكية، ولكنه أمر بخلعها ليباشر تراب الأرض المقدسة فيناله بركتها) (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r6.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Najih explains the instruction as bringing Moses’ feet into contact with the valley’s blessing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p366/r6.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح: (يقول: أفض بقدميك إلى بركة الوادي) (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r1.claim: Al-Wādī al-muqaddas means the purified valley.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إنك بالواد المقدس} أي: المطهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through ʿAṭāʾ, says the valley was sanctified twice; ʿIkrima shares this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (قدسته مرتين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r3.claim: In al-Wālibī’s transmission, Ibn Abbas glosses al-muqaddas as blessed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r4.claim: The commentary refers readers to its discussion of the sacred land at 5:21.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r4.anchor: وذكرنا الكلام في هذا عند قوله: {ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Ṭuwā is the valley’s name, a view shared by all exegetes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r6.claim: Al-Hasan instead takes Ṭuwā to mean that it was blessed twice.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r7.claim: On al-Hasan’s interpretation, Ṭuwā is a verbal noun from ṭawaytuhu ṭawā, meaning I folded it twice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r7.anchor: فعلى هذا (طوى) مصدر من قولك: طويته طوى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r8.speaker: عدي بن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r8.claim: The line by ʿAdī ibn Zayd uses ṭawā for something repeated upon the speaker.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r8.anchor: قال عدي بن زيد (¬8): أعاذل إن اللوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r9.claim: The author prefers the first view: Ṭuwā is the valley’s proper name.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r10.claim: Abū Isḥāq lists four forms: Ṭuwā with ṭāʾ vocalized either way, each with or without declension.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r10.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ويجوز فيه أربعة أوجه، -يعني من القراءة -: ضم الطاء، وكسرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains declension by treating the name as masculine on the faʿal pattern, like Ḥaṭam and Ṣarad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r11.anchor: فمن أجرى فلأنه مذكر سمي بمذكر على فعل نحو: حطم وصرد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r12.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r12.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains nondeclension either as an altered form like ʿUmar or as a feminine place-name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r12.anchor: ومن لم يجري ترك صرفه من جهتين أحدهما: أن يكون معدولا عن طاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r13.claim: With kasra, Ṭuwā follows forms such as maʿā and ḍila; without tanwīn it is a place-name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r13.anchor: قال: وإذا كسر طوى فهو مثل: معى، وضلع.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r14.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows declension as a masculine valley-name or as an adjective meaning twice-sanctified, with either vowel like siwan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r14.anchor: وقال أبو علي: (الصرف من وجهين أحدهما: أن يجعل اسم الوادي فيصرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r15.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r15.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains nondeclension either by a feminine locality bearing a masculine name or by alteration like ʿUmar, even from an unattested base.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p369/r15.anchor: قال: ومن لم يصرف احتمل أمرين أحدهما: أن يكون (طوى) اسما لبقعة أو أرض وهو مذكر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.claim: Qatāda says Moses' two sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; Moses removed them and approached.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r1.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت. فخلعهما ثم أتى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r2.anchor: إنك بالواد المقدس طوى} [طه: 12] والمقدس: المبارك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r3.claim: Qatāda says the valley was blessed twice and was named Ṭuwā.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r3.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: قدس مرتين، أي بورك مرتين، واسمه طوى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r4.speaker: عكرمة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r4.claim: ʿIkrima explains Ṭuwā as meaning to tread the valley.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r4.anchor: الفرات بن سلمان، عن عبد الكريم الجزري، عن عكرمة قال: {طوى} [طه: 12] يعني: إيطأ الوادي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the valley was blessed twice.

QASHANI:20:12-13/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r1.claim: After turning spiritually toward holiness, Moses must sever his remaining attachment to the sandals, which sinks the heart's lower aspect, called the breast; the author connects this to 73:8.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r1.anchor: وتبتل إليه تبتيلا [المزمل، الآية:8] فكأنه بقيت علاقته معهما والتعلق بهما يسوخ قدمه

QASHANI:20:12-13/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r2.claim: The sacred valley Tuwa is the spirit-world, purified of material attachments; the stages of the dominion and the heavens and earth are folded beneath it.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r2.anchor: عالم الروح المنزه عن آثار التعلق وهيئات اللواحق والعلائق المادية المسمى طوى

QASHANI:20:12-13/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r3.claim: He endorses the view that the sandals were made from the hide of an un-tanned dead donkey.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r3.anchor: ولقد صدق من قال: أمر بخلعهما لكونهما من جلد حمار ميت غير مدبوغ.

QASHANI:20:12-13/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r4.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:20:12-13/r4.claim: An anonymous report says Satan whispered that the caller was Satan; Moses recognized the Merciful's call because he heard through all six directions and all his limbs.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r4.anchor: وقيل: لما نودي وسوس إليه الشيطان: إنك تنادى من شيطان! فقال: أفرق به، إني أسمع من جميع الجهات الست

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r1.claim: The command to remove the sandals means renouncing both kinds of one's actions and erasing paired states—nearness and distance, union and separation, annihilation and subsistence—from one's witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r1.anchor: تبرأ عن نوعي أفعالك ، وامح عن الشهود جنسي أحوالك من قرب وبعد ، ووصل وفصل

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r2.claim: Moses is to take on God's attribute and be through God, until he is stripped of self and overwhelmed by what he witnesses.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r2.anchor: وكن بوصفنا ؛ فإنما أنت بحقنا . أثبته في أحواله حتى كان كالمجرد عن جملته ، المصطلم عن شواهده

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r3.claim: The sacred valley is free of defects; the precincts of divine self-sufficiency transcend blemish and ornament, for God's sovereign flashes overpower everything.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r3.anchor: أي إنك بالوادي المقدس عن الأعلال ؛ وساحات الصمدية تجل عن كل شين ، وإيمان وزين

BURHAN:v2p308/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p308/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p308/r1.claim: The passage’s tenth rhetorical mode is a metonymy that conveys the gist of a sentence whose apparent wording is not intended literally, without assigning each word a literal or figurative sense.
BURHAN:v2p308/r1.anchor: عاشرها ان يعمد إلى جملة ورد معناها على خلاف الظاهر

BURHAN:v2p308/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p308/r10.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
BURHAN:v2p308/r10.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi objects that this broad metonymic method opens the door to esoteric reinterpretations, such as reading Moses’ command to remove his shoes as total devotion rather than an actual command about shoes.
BURHAN:v2p308/r10.anchor: وقد اعترض الامام فخر الدين على ذلك

SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.claim: Moses recognized God's call as it enveloped every hair from every direction; awe and majesty confirmed it, and the divine self-identification left him stunned and annihilated. God alone bears and answers His address; Moses is its intermediary locus.
SULAMI:v1p436#3/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : قيل لموسى عليه السلام : كيف عرفت أن النداء هو نداء الحق ؟ فقال : لأني أقياني وشملني

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r1.speaker: أبو سفيان
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r1.claim: Moses removes his sandals so his feet receive the valley's blessing and the valley receives the blessing of his feet.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو سفيان : اخلع نعليك ليصيب قدمك بركة الوادي والوادي بركة قدمك .

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r2.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r2.claim: Shedding everything of oneself brings one wholly to God, where being and nonbeing meet and one's reports and actions are realized as God's.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r2.anchor: قال الشبلي : اخلع الكل منك تصل إلينا بالكل ، فتكون ولا تكون ، فتحقق في عين الجمع بكون أخبارك عنا ،

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r3.claim: Taking off the sandals means turning the heart away from the created world after receiving this address.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اخلع نعليك أعرض بقلبك عن الكون فلا تنظر إليه بعد هذا الخطاب .

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r4.claim: The sandals signify the lower self; the sacred valley is the pearl-like religion of being emptied of self and standing with God through one's religion.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : النعل النفس ، والواد المقدس دين المرجان

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r5.claim: The command to remove the sandals comes because Moses is under the sight of the One in whom he exists.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r5.anchor: وقيل اخلع نعليك فإنك بعين موجودك

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r6.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r6.claim: Moses should sever his attachments because he is beneath God's eyes.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r6.anchor: وقال جعفر : اقطع عنك العلائق فإنك بأعيننا .

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r7.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r7.claim: He should shed the stations of separation and connection: the sacred valley purifies him of states and returns him to the One who transforms them.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : اخلع نعليك أي : أسقط عنك محل الفصل والوصل فقد حصلت في الواد المقدس

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r8.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r8.claim: A wordplay on Tuwa says God folds away the carpet of disobedience from Moses' heart in the sacred valley.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r8.anchor: قيل في قوله : واد المقدس طوى . أي : أطوى عنك بساط المخالفات فقد حصلت في هذا الوادي

SULAMI:v1p436#4/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r9.claim: Removing the sandals means relinquishing the power of connection and separation; Moses is in the valley of solitude with God alone.
SULAMI:v1p436#4/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : في قوله : ﴿ اخلع نعليك ﴾ أي : انزع عنك قوة الاتصال والانفصال إنك بالواد المقدس

ITQAN:v2p320/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p320/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p320/r1.claim: The blessed valley is named Tuwa.

ITQAN:v4p377/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p377/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Tuwa as the name of a valley.
ITQAN:v4p377/r5.anchor: وطوى اسم الوادي كما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v4p377/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p377/r6.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas explains the name by saying Moses traversed it at night.
ITQAN:v4p377/r6.anchor: وأخرج من وجه آخر عنه أنه سمى طوى لأن موسى طواه ليلا

ITQAN:v4p377/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r7.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v4p377/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says Tuwa is a valley in Palestine, named because it was sanctified twice.
ITQAN:v4p377/r7.anchor: وأخرج عن الحسن قال هو واد بفلسطين قيل له طوى لأنه قدس مرتين

ITQAN:v4p377/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r8.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
ITQAN:v4p377/r8.claim: Mubashshir ibn Ubayd says Tuwa is a valley at Ayla, blessed twice.
ITQAN:v4p377/r8.anchor: وأخرج عن مبشر بن عبيد قال هو واد بأيلة طوي بالبركة مرتين

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read إني with fatḥa, supplying an implicit ب because نادى takes this preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالفتح، على تقدير الباء بأني؛ لأن النداء يوصل بها

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r2.claim: The author cites an unnamed poet, recited by al-Farisi, whose ناديت باسم construction illustrates connecting نادى with ب.

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows the fatḥa to mean 'because'; the author says this is not apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r3.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية أن يكون بمعنى لأجل. وليس بظاهر.

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r4.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r4.claim: The remaining readers use kasra, analyzed either with an omitted قول by Basran grammarians or because نادى means 'say' for the Kufans.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r4.anchor: والباقون بالكسر: إما على إضمار القول كما هو رأي البصريين، وإما لأن النداء في معنى القول عند الكوفيين.

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r5.claim: أنا can be a subject with what follows as its predicate, an emphasis for the object pronoun, or a separator.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r5.anchor: قوله: { أنا } يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ، وما بعده خبره، والجملة خبر " إن ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r6.speaker: الكوفيون وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r6.claim: The Kufans and Ibn ʿAmir read طوى with ḍamma and tanwin, treating it as a place name and therefore fully declinable.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r6.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون وابن عامر " طوى " بضم الطاء والتنوين.

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r7.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r7.claim: The other readers use ḍamma without tanwin; the author offers feminine place-name, lexical shift, or foreign-name analyses for its nondeclension.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r7.anchor: والباقون بضمها من غير تنوين. وقرأ الحسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن بكسر الطاء

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r8.claim: The nondeclined form may also be treated as shifted to the pattern فعل, like عمر and زفر, or as foreign, in either case indeclinable.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r8.anchor: الثاني: أنه منعه للعدل إلى فعل، وإن لم يعرف اللفظ المعدول عنه، وجعله كعمر وزفر.

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r9.speaker: الحسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r9.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Aʿmash, Abu Haywa, and Ibn Muhaysin read طوى with kasra and tanwin; the kasra reflects a place name.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن بكسر الطاء منونا

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r10.speaker: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r10.claim: Abu Zayd from Abu ʿAmr reads طوى with kasra and no tanwin; it is like عِنَب if a noun or عُدى and سُوى if an adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r10.anchor: وابو زيد عن أبي عمرو بكسرها غير منون

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r11.speaker: الحسن البصري
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r11.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri understands طوى as 'twice' or 'repeatedly': the place was manifested twice, and the word is a verbal noun of sanctifying twice.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r11.anchor: وعن الحسن البصري أنه بمعنى الثنى بالكسر والقصر، والثنى: المكرر مرتين، فيكون معنى هذه القراءة أنه ظهر مرتين،

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r12.speaker: عيسى بن عمر والضحاك
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r12.claim: ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and al-Dahhak read طاوي اذهب.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r12.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر والضحاك " طاوي اذهب ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r13.claim: طوى may be an appositive or بدل for الوادي, or nominative with an implicit subject, or accusative with an implicit أعني.
SAMIN-DURR:20:12/r13.anchor: و " طوى ": إما بدل من الوادي، أو عطف بيان له، أو مرفوع على إضمار مبتدأ، أو منصوب على إضمار أعني.

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r1.claim: Ṭuwā is the name of the valley.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r1.anchor: وقوله: (طوى). اسم الوادي، ويجوز فيه أربعة أوجه

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r2.claim: Four forms are allowed: Ṭuwā with initial ḍamma, with or without nunation, and with initial kasra, with or without nunation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r2.anchor: ويجوز فيه أربعة أوجه: طوى - بضم

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r3.claim: When nunated, Ṭuwā is a masculine valley name on the pattern fuʿal, like Ḥuṭam and Ṣurad.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r3.anchor: فمن نونه فهو اسم الوادي، وهو مذكر

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r4.claim: A non-nunated form may be diptote because it is shifted from Ṭāʾ, like ʿUmar from ʿĀmir, or because it is a place name.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r4.anchor: ومن لم ينونه ترك صرفه من جهتين

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r5.claim: With initial kasra and nunation it declines like maʿan or ḍilʿ; without nunation it is treated as a place name.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r5.anchor: والجهة الأخرى أن يكون اسما للبقعة كما قال الله عز وجل

ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r1.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r1.claim: Some commentators take tuwan or tuwa as the proper name of the hallowed valley.
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r1.anchor: the word tuwan (or tuwa) is the name of the "hallowed valley"

ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r2.claim: Asad prefers Zamakhshari's reading of tuwan or tuwa as “twice,” making the valley twice hallowed because God's voice was heard there and Moses was raised there to prophethood.
ASAD-NOTES:20:11#n9/r2.anchor: Zamakhshari explains it, more convincingly, as meaning "twice" (from tuwan or Owan, "twice done")

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r1.claim: Ṭā Hā directly addresses Moses, instructs him in worship and prayer, and recalls his life in direct speech; this suits the personal wording I am your Lord, unlike the narrative treatment in al-Qaṣaṣ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p108/r1.anchor: فإنه لم يذكر توجيهاً له أو إرشاداً لعبادته في النمل، ولا في القصص فلم يأمره بعبادة أو صلاة أو تكليف خاص بشأنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p107/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p107/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p107/r2.claim: Ṭā Hā says your Lord because its scene first directs Moses personally to worship and prayer; al-Naml and al-Qaṣaṣ use Lord of the worlds, and al-Naml adds the names al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥakīm.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p107/r2.anchor: أنه في سورة طه كان الخطاب والتوجيه لموسى عليه السلام أولاً فعلّمه وأرشده

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r1.claim: Ta-Ha narrates God's address to Moses directly and gives him worship and guidance, unlike Naml and Qasas; therefore “I am your Lord” suits Ta-Ha's direct address.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p87/r1.anchor: في حين كان الكلام في سورة طه بصورة الخطاب. فناسب أن يقول له في طه: "أنا ربّك" بخلاف ما في النمل والقصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r4.claim: Ta-Ha uses particular lordship because God first addresses and instructs Moses, commanding worship and prayer, then promises signs and recalls His favor; Naml and Qasas say “Lord of the worlds.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p86/r4.anchor: في سورة طه كان الخطاب والتوجيه لموسى عليه السلام أولا فعلمه وأرشده فقال له

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the hamza in annī with fatḥa, and its yāʾ with fatḥa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: (أني) بفتح الألف والياء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r2.claim: Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read innī with kasra; Nafi opens the yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: إني بكسر الألف، وفتح نافع الياء .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r3.claim: The kasra best fits direct quoted speech, as do the following quoted statements ‘I am God’ and ‘I have chosen you.’
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r3.anchor: من كسر فلأن الكلام حكاية، كأنه نودي فقيل: يا موسى إني أنا ربك، والكسر أشبه بما بعد مما هو حكاية،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r4.claim: With fatḥa, the sense is ‘He was called with the words that I am your Lord’; Arabic can connect nādā to a statement with a preposition, as the cited poetry shows.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r4.anchor: ومن فتح كان المعنى: نودي بكذا، ونادى قد يوصل بحرف الجر، قال:

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r5.claim: In the passive construction, neither quoted clause can itself be the deputy subject because clauses cannot fill that role; the previously mentioned Mūsā could do so.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p218#2/r5.anchor: وينبغي أن يكون في نودي ضمير يقوم مقام الفاعل، لأنه لا يجوز أن يقوم واحد من قولك: يا موسى ولا إني أنا ربك مقام الفاعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read Ṭuwā without declension and with ṭāʾ ḍamma, as at 79:16–17.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو: (طوى وأنا) غير مجراة والطاء مضمومة وفي النازعات [16، 17] مثله.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r2.claim: Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read Ṭuwā as declinable, with ṭāʾ ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: طوى مجراة مضمومة الطاء .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r3.speaker: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r3.claim: Abu Zayd transmits from Abu Amr the form Ṭuwā and glosses it as a land or place.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r3.anchor: وروى أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو: (طوى) وقال: هي أرض.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r4.claim: Declension is possible if Ṭuwā is a masculine valley name, or if it is an adjective meaning sanctified twice, like thanā and sawāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r4.anchor: فمن صرف فمن وجهين أحدهما: أن يجعله اسم الوادي فيصرف لأنه سمى مذكرا بمذكر

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r5.claim: Nondeclension is possible if Ṭuwā is a place or land name, or an analogical indeclinable form like ʿUmar even without an attested source form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r5.anchor: ومن لم يصرف احتمل أمرين: أحدهما: أن يكون اسما لبقعة أو أرض، وهو مذكر، فهو بمنزلة امرأة سميتها بحجر،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r6.speaker: مجاهدا
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r6.claim: A transmitted gloss, tentatively attributed to Mujahid, says to go barefoot toward the valley’s blessed place; Ṭuwā may be either declinable or indeclinable.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r6.anchor: قال: يقول: امض بقدميك إلى بركة الوادي، أظنه- يعني مجاهدا- طوى، مصروف وغير مصروف،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r7.claim: Thanā means something not occurring for the first time; the related thanāʾ are those who follow the lords, called al-badʾ because they lead in important matters.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p219/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: ومعنى ثنى وثنى: الذين يثنى بهم بعد السادة، لأنهم قالوا للسيد: البدء، من حيث بدئ بهم فيما يهم من الأمور.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r2.claim: Opening the hamza makes the clause governed by “he called”; kasra starts an independent clause with no syntactic position as its particle introduces a new statement.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r2.anchor: يقرأ بفتح الهمزة وكسرها فالحجة لمن فتحها أنه أوقع عليها نودي

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r4.claim: The uninflected, sukūn form treats Ṭuwā as a feminine place name; definiteness plus femininity make it diptote, and the author prefers it to match the preceding verse endings.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r4.anchor: فالحجة لمن أسكن ولم يصرف أنه جعله اسم بقعة فاجتمع فيه التعريف والتأنيث وهما فرعان لأن التنكير أصل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r5.claim: The inflected form with tanwin treats Ṭuwā as a masculine valley name, so it lacks the pair of causes that would prevent declension.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r5.anchor: والحجة لمن أجراه ونونه أنه اسم واد مذكرا فصرفه لأنه لم تجتمع فيه علتان تمنعانه الصرف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r6.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r6.claim: Some grammarians derive Ṭuwā by alteration from Ṭāwin, like ʿUmar from ʿĀmir; the author doubts another wāw noun has undergone this alteration.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240/r6.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين هو معدول عن طاو كما عدل عمر عن عامر فإن صح ذلك فليس في ذوات الواو اسم عدل

NASHR:v2p319#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p319#2/r1.claim: In إني أنا ربك, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja'far read the initial hamza with fatḥa; the others use kasra.
NASHR:v2p319#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر بفتح الهمزة

NASHR:v2p319#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر والكوفيون
NASHR:v2p319#2/r2.claim: Ibn Amir and the Kufans give طوى tanwin in both Taha and al-Naziat; the remaining readers omit tanwin.

NASHR:v2p322/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r5.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p322/r5.claim: For five yāʾs of annexation—إني آنست, إني أنا ربك, إنني أنا الله, لنفسي اذهب, and في ذكري—the two Medinese, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read the yāʾ open.
NASHR:v2p322/r5.anchor: إني آنست، إني أنا ربك، إنني أنا الله، لنفسي اذهب، في ذكري اذهبا

NASHR:v2p322/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p322/r10.claim: By Abu Ja'far's general rule, the yāʾs should be open where he cuts the hamza, but Ibn al-Jazari found no explicit transmission for that inference.
NASHR:v2p322/r10.anchor: مذهب أبي جعفر فتحها لمن قطع الهمزة عنه، ولكني لم أجده منصوصا

QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#1/r1.claim: The final yāʾ in inniya is pronounced with fatḥa, an alternative canonical pronunciation without change in meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#1/r1.anchor: Final yāʾ pronounced with fatḥa — an alternative canonical reading that adds phonetic openness to the pronoun ending

QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#2/r1.speaker: ḥf
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#2/r1.claim: Reading anna rather than inna makes the clause subordinate, meaning that I am your Lord, with an elided main clause such as Know.
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:1#2/r1.anchor: Hamza changed from kasra to fatḥa: shifts from inna (emphatic particle) to anna (complementizer ""that"")

QIRAAT-ER:20:12:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:9#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:9#1/r1.claim: The ten-reader form restores final yāʾ to wādī, while the shortened form follows standard rasm; the difference has no semantic effect.
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:9#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ restored (bi-l-wādī) vs shortened form (bi-l-wādi) — the 10-reader variant restores the final yāʾ

QIRAAT-ER:20:12:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:11#1/r1.speaker: Tnw
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:11#1/r1.claim: Without tanwīn, Ṭuwā is treated as a diptote proper name, foreign or feminine, that rejects nunation.
QIRAAT-ER:20:12:11#1/r1.anchor: Without tanwīn: read as diptote proper noun (mamūʿ min al-ṣarf) — the name Ṭuwā is treated as a definite foreign or feminine proper noun

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r1.claim: Qatāda says Moses’ sandals were donkey hide and he was told to remove them because the valley was sanctified twice.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فاخلع نعليك ﴾ قال كانتا من جلد حمار فقيل له اخلعهما فالقدس قدس بها مرتين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r2.claim: Qatāda says Ṭuwā is the name of the valley.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فاخلع نعليك ﴾ قال كانتا من جلد حمار فقيل له اخلعهما فالقدس قدس بها مرتين وطوى اسم الوادي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r3.speaker: كعب الأحبار
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r3.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār says the sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r3.anchor: عن كعب الأحبار قال كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r4.speaker: كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r4.claim: Kaʿb says Moses was commanded to remove the dead donkey-hide sandals so that his feet would directly touch the sacred ground.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r4.anchor: عن أبي قلابة عن كعب قال هل تدرون لم قال الله لموسى اخلع نعليك قال إنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت فأمر أن يباشر القدس بقدميه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r5.speaker: ابن الزبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Israelite leaders removed their sandals whenever they reached Ṭuwā.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r5.anchor: عن ابن الزبير قال كانت الأئمة من بني إسرائيل إذا بلغوا طوى خلعوا نعالهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r6.speaker: أشياخ ابن جريج
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj’s elders relate that Tubbaʿ dismounted at Marra, removed his sandals to honor the sanctuary, and walked to the House.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r6.anchor: عن أشياخهم أن تبعا لما بلغ مرا نزل عن دابته وخلع نعليه تعظيما للحرم ثم مشى حتى أتى البيت

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r7.speaker: علي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r7.claim: ʿAlī also says Moses’ sandals were donkey hide and that he was told to remove them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p15#4/r7.anchor: عن علي قال كانتا من جلد حمار فقيل له اخلعهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r1.claim: The majority read the hamza of أن with kasra, treating the words as direct speech: I am your Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r1.anchor: ولذلك كسرت همزة أن في قراءة الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the hamza with fatḥa, supplying bi; the resulting prepositional phrase attaches to نودي.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابو عمرو بفتحها على تقدير حرف الجر أي بانى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
