ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r3.claim: Abu Ali cites poetry for allowing a vocative to be introduced by a preposition; al-Alusi finds this parsing awkward when the vocative intervenes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r3.anchor: أنشد اب على : ناديت باسم ربيعة بن مكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r4.claim: The alternative taking the preposition as causal and attaching it to the following imperative is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r4.anchor: على تقدير حرف التعليل وتعلقه بفعل الأمر بعد وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi prefers supplying أعلم: I know that I am your Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r5.anchor: واختير أن الكلام على تقدير العلم أي أعلم انى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r6.claim: Repeating the first-person pronoun reinforces identification, establishes recognition, and removes doubt.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r6.anchor: وتكرير ضمير المتكلم لتاكيد الدلالة وتحقيق المعرفة واماطة الشبهة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi favors Moses recognizing the speaker through knowledge God created in him necessarily; other views appeal to a prior or subsequent miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r7.anchor: واستظهر أن علمه عليه السلام بأن الذي ناداه هو الله تعالى حصل له بالضرورة خلقا منه تعالى فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r8.claim: An ungraded report says Moses identified the divine voice because he heard it from every direction and through every bodily organ; al-Alusi doubts its reliability and the Satan episode's plausibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r8.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : انا عرفت أنه كلام الله تعالى بانى اسمعه من

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r9.claim: The Muʿtazila require inference from a miracle: necessary knowledge of God's speech would entail necessary knowledge of the Creator and remove Moses from moral responsibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r9.anchor: والمعتزلة اوجبوا أن يكون العلم بالاستدلال بالخرق ولم يجوزوا أن يكون بالضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r10.claim: Some say there is no need to identify what the miracle that established the speaker's identity was.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لا حاجة بنا إلى أن نعرف ذلك الخالق ما هو

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r11.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r11.claim: A report from Wahb says Moses answered the call instinctively, heard it everywhere without seeing its place, and was told God was near him in every direction and nearer than his self; Moses then became certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r11.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وغيره عن وهب عليه السلام لما اشتدا عليه الهول نودى من الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r12.claim: The report is compatible with Salafi and Sufi approaches, but certainty from attributes seemingly unique to God remains vulnerable to satanic suggestion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r12.anchor: ولا يخفى تخريج هذا الأثر على مذهب السلف ومذهب الصوفية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r13.speaker: جماعة من أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r13.claim: A Sunni group takes the account to mean Moses directly heard God's verbal speech without an intermediary, and holds that speech eternal.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r13.anchor: ظاهر في أن موسى عليه السلام سمع الكلام اللفظى منه تعالى بلا واسطه ولذا اختص عليه السلام باسم الكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r14.speaker: جماعة من أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r14.claim: They answer that successive letters imply temporal succession only when speech uses an instrument such as a tongue; without an organ it may occur all at once.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r14.anchor: لأنه لا يوجد بعضه إلا بتقضى بعض آخر بأنه إنما يلزم من التلفظ بآلة وجارحة وهى اللسان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r15.speaker: أهل ما وراء النهر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r15.claim: Sunni scholars of Transoxiana who affirm eternal divine speech hold that the speech Moses heard was a created sound in the tree.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r15.anchor: ولذا زعم أهل ما وراء النهر من أهل السنة القائلين بقدم الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r16.speaker: أهل البدعة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r16.claim: The groups al-Alusi calls innovators agree that verbal divine speech is originated, but differ over whether temporal events may subsist in God; those denying this say the sound was created in a body.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p167#2/r16.anchor: وأهل البدعه اجمعوا على أن الكلام اللفظى حادث بيد أن منهم من جوز قيام الحوادث به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r1.speaker: الأشعري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r1.claim: Al-Ashʿari says God made Moses hear inner speech, neither letters nor sound and beyond rational comprehension; an explanation describes spiritual reception later rendered as perceived words, like speech in a dream.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r1.anchor: وقال إلا شعري : إن الله تعالى أسمع موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r2.claim: Some explain Moses' experience as spiritual reception of inner speech, which intellect and the common sense represent in familiar word forms, as in dreams.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r2.anchor: تلقى ذلك الكلام تلقيا روحانيا كما تتلقا الملائكة عليهم السلام كلامه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r3.claim: Al-Alusi finds the suggestion that Satan recognized Moses' hearing state by observation speculative and unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r3.anchor: ووجه وقوف الشيطان المار بالخبر الذي سمعت ما فيه على هذا بأنه يحتمل أن يكون كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r4.claim: The command means to take the sandals off one's feet; نعل is the familiar feminine noun, with diminutive نعيلة.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r4.anchor: ازلهما من رجليك والنعل معروفة وهى مؤنثه يقال في تصغيرها نعيلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r5.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r5.claim: Al-Farra cites poetry using نعل with a fatḥa on its second radical, supporting that lexical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r5.anchor: نعل : بفتح العين أنشد الفراء : له نعل لا يطبى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r6.speaker: الصادق وعكرمة وقتادة والسدى ومقاتل والضحاك والكلبى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r6.claim: These authorities report that Moses' sandals were made from the hide of an unburied, untanned donkey.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r6.anchor: لما انهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت غير مدبوغ كما روى عن الصادق رضى الله تعالى عنه وعكرمة وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r7.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r7.claim: A report transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, which al-Alusi calls unusual, describes Moses in wool garments and a small cap, with sandals of donkey hide.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r7.anchor: أخرج الترمذى بسنده عن النبى ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ) قال : كان على موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r8.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير وابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r8.claim: These authorities say the sandals were made from the hide of a ritually slaughtered cow; Moses was told to remove them so his feet could touch the blessed valley.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r8.anchor: وعن الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد ابن جبير وابن جريج انهما كانتا من جلد بقرة ذكيت ولكن أمر عليه السلام بخلعهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r9.speaker: الأصم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r9.claim: Al-Asamm says going barefoot is more humble and proper, as righteous predecessors circumambulated the Kaaba barefoot; al-Alusi notes this conflicts with reports favoring prayer in sandals.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169/r9.anchor: لأن الحفوة ادخل في التواضع وحسن الادب ولذلك كان السلف الصالحون يطوفون بالكعبة حافين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r1.claim: Abu Muslim says Moses was commanded to remove the sandals because God had secured him from fear and stationed him in a purified place; he wore them against dirt and insects.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : لأنه تعالى امنه من الخوف واوقفه بالموضع الطاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r2.claim: An allegorical interpretation takes the sandals to mean whatever one relies on, so Moses must empty his heart of family and wealth, or of this world and the next; al-Alusi calls this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : المعنى فرغ قلبك من الأهل والمال وقيل : من الدنيا والاخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r3.claim: The ف orders the removal as a consequence of the preceding declaration of God's lordship, which motivates the command.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r3.anchor: والفاء لترتيب الأمر على ما قبلها فان ربوبيته تعالى له عليه السلام من موجبات الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r4.claim: The sacred valley clause explains the reason for removing the sandals: the place itself is honored and pure.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r4.anchor: تعليل لموجب الخلع المؤمور به وبيان لسبب ورود الأمر بذلك من شرف البقعة وقدسها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r5.claim: An unspecified report says Moses removed the sandals and cast them behind the valley when commanded.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r5.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام حين أمر خلعهما والقاهما وراء الوادى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r6.speaker: الكوفيون وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r6.claim: The Kufans and Ibn ʿAmir read طوى with ḍamma and tanwīn; others also differ over its vowel and tanwīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الكوفييون وابن عامر بضمها منونا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r7.speaker: حسن والأعمش وأبو حيوة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو السمال وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r7.claim: These readers pronounce طوى with kasra and tanwīn; Abu Zayd from Abu Amr reads it with kasra but without tanwīn.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ حسن والأعمش وابو حيوة وابن أبى إسحاق وابو السمال وابن محيصن بكسرها منونه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi says طوى is most plausibly the valley's proper name in every reading; it is appositive or explanatory, and tanwīn reflects place versus region interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r8.anchor: وهو علم لذلك الوادى فيكون بدلا أو عطف بيان ومن نونه فعلى تأويل المكان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r9.claim: Another analysis makes uninflected ḍamma طوى a diptote because of proper-name status and either alteration, like Zafar and Qutham, or foreignness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r9.anchor: وقيل ( طوى ) المضموم الطاء الغير منون ممنوع من الصرف للعلمية والعدل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r10.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r10.claim: Qutrub says طوى means that a portion of the night was sanctified, the very hour Moses was called, making it adverbial to المقدس.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r10.anchor: وقال قطرب : يقال طوى من الليل أي قدس لك ساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r11.speaker: الكرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r11.claim: Al-Kirmani's Wonders reportedly treats طوى as an Arabized word meaning night, apparently following Qutrub.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r11.anchor: وفي العجائب للكرمانى وقيل : هو معرب معناه ليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r12.claim: One view takes طوى as a man's name in Hebrew and thus as a vocative.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : هو رجل بالعبرانية وكانه على هذا منادى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r13.claim: Al-Hasan reads طوى with kasra and tanwīn as a verbal noun meaning twice, attached to المقدس as sanctified repeatedly, or to نودي as called twice.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن : طوى بكسر الطاء والتنوين مصدر كثنى لفظا ومعنى وهو عنده معمول للمقدس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r14.speaker: ابن السيد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r14.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid derives طوى from folding or doing something twice; al-Tabarsi cites ʿAdi ibn Zayd's poetry for this sense, while al-Raghib notes its initial vowel may vary.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r14.anchor: وقال ابن السيد : أنه ما يطوى من جلد الحية ويقال : فعل الشئ طوى أي مرتين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r15.claim: Despite the alternative etymologies, al-Alusi considers the valley's name the clearest reading throughout.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p169#2/r15.anchor: ولا يخفى عليك أن الاظهر كونه اسما للوادى في جميع القراءات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r1.claim: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read annī with fatḥa, meaning that Moses was called with the words that God is his Lord; the others read innī with kasra as direct speech after the call.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، وابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، "أني" بفتح الألف، على معنى: نودي بأني. وقرأ الآخرون بكسر الألف، أي: نودي، فقيل: إني أنا ربك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r2.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r2.claim: Wahb recounts that Moses heard a voice from the tree, asked where the speaker was, and heard that He was above, with, before, behind, and nearer than Moses himself; Moses recognized this as fitting only God and believed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r2.anchor: قال وهب نودي من الشجرة، فقيل: يا موسى، فأجاب سريعا لا يدري من دعاه، فقال: إني أسمع صوتك ولا أرى مكانك فأين أنت؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet from Ibn Masud says the sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r3.anchor: ما روي عن ابن مسعود مرفوعا في قوله: {فاخلع نعليك} قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r4.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say Moses was told to remove his sandals so his feet would touch the holy earth and receive its blessing, since it had been sanctified twice; he threw them behind the valley.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p266#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: أمر بخلع النعلين ليباشر بقدمه تراب الأرض المقدسة، فيناله بركتها لأنها قدست مرتين،

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read إني with fatḥa, understood as بأني; the remaining readers use kasra, with القول understood or the call treated as speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r2.anchor: فتحه ابن كثير وأبو عمرو أي بأني وكسره الباقون

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r3.claim: The pronoun is repeated for emphasis and confirmation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.claim: It is said that Moses wondered who was speaking; after hearing God identify Himself, Satan suggested it might be a devil, but Moses recognized God's speech because he heard it from every direction and through every limb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r4.anchor: قيل إنه لما نودي قال: من المتكلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.claim: The account points to Moses receiving God's speech spiritually, then its representation reaching his body and common sense without limitation to one organ or direction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r5.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام تلقى من ربه كلامه تلقيا روحانيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.claim: Removing the sandals may signify humility and decorum, as early Muslims circumambulated barefoot.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r6.anchor: أمره بذلك لأن الحفوة تواضع وأدب ولذلك طاف السلف حافين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the sandals were unclean because they were made of untanned donkey hide.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r7.anchor: وقيل لنجاسة نعليه فإنهما كانتا من جلد حمار غير مدبوغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.claim: A figurative interpretation reads the command as emptying the heart of family and possessions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r8.anchor: وقيل معناه فرغ قلبك من الأهل والمال

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.claim: The holy valley explains why the place should be treated with reverence; المقدس can bear both senses discussed for holiness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.anchor: تعليل للأمر باحترام البقعة والمقدس يحتمل المعنيين

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.claim: طوى is an explanatory apposition for the valley; Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read it with tanwīn, construing it as a place name.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.anchor: عطف بيان للوادي ونونه ابن عامر والكوفيون بتأويل المكان

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.claim: Alternatively, طوى is like ثنى, a verbal noun from folding, describing two calls or a place sanctified twice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.anchor: وقيل هو كثني من الطي مصدر

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says Moses was told to remove his sandals so the soles of his feet would touch the blessed earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فاخلع نعليك} قال كي تمس راحة قدميك الأرض الطيبة

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd rebukes Abū Mūsā for removing his sandals as though in the holy valley, recalling that he saw the Prophet pray in socks and sandals.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r2.anchor: قال له ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: - لم خلعت نعليك أبالواد المقدس أنت لقد رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي في الخفين والنعلين

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the sacred valley as blessed and identifies Ṭuwā as the valley’s name.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس} قال: المبارك {طوى} قال: اسم الوادي

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r4.claim: ʿIkrima explains “the sacred valley” as the pure valley.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة - رضي الله عنه - في قوله: {بالواد المقدس} قال: الطاهر

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan locates the valley in Palestine and says it was sanctified twice.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {بالواد المقدس} قال: واد بلفلسطين قدس مرتين

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās connects Ṭuwā with traversing the holy land’s valley at night, using the expression for crossing or folding a valley and rising to its upper part.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله: {بالواد المقدس طوى} يعني الأرض المقدسى وذلك أنه مر بواديها ليلا فطوي يقال: طويت وادي كذا وكذا والطاوي من الليل

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r7.claim: Mujāhid agrees that the sacred valley is blessed and that Ṭuwā is its name.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إنك بالواد المقدس} قال: المبارك: {طوى} قال: اسم الوادي

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r8.speaker: مبشر بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r8.claim: Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd reports the form Ṭuwā without nunation, identifies it as a valley at Aylah, and says it was blessed twice.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r8.anchor: عن مبشر بن عبيد {طوى} بغير نون واد بإيلة زعم أنه طوي بالبركة مرتين

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses Ṭuwā as “the valley was folded.”
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {طوى} قال: طا الوادي

DURR-FULL:v5p559/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains Ṭuwā through Moses entering the blessed valley barefoot, like one entering the Kaaba barefoot; Mujāhid instead treats it as the valley’s proper name.
DURR-FULL:v5p559/r10.anchor: يقول: من بركة الوادي هذا قول سعيد بن جبير قال: وكان مجاهد رضي الله عنه يقول: {طوى} اسم الوادي

DURR-FULL:v5p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r1.claim: Qatāda says the valley was sanctified twice and was named Ṭuwā.
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {بالواد المقدس طوى} قال: واد قدس مرتين واسمه {طوى}

DURR-FULL:v5p560/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r2.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim reads Ṭuwā with the ṭāʾ in the nominative and nunation.
DURR-FULL:v5p560/r2.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {طوى} برفع الطاء وبنون فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r1.claim: The preceding phrase can mean “because I am your Lord,” and نودي can take a prepositional complement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r1.anchor: على معنى «لأجل أني» أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك، ونودي قد توصل بحرف الجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r2.claim: The verb نودي may be used with a preposition, supported by a line of Abu ʿAli's poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r2.anchor: ونودي قد توصل بحرف الجر وأنشد أبو علي:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r3.claim: One group says Moses had sandals made from the hide of a dead donkey and was told to remove the impurity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r3.anchor: فقالت فرقة كانتا من جلد حمار ميت فأمر بطرح النجاسة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r4.claim: Another group says the sandals were from properly slaughtered cowhide and were removed so Moses could receive the valley's blessing and touch its soil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل كانت نعلاه من جلد بقرة ذكي لكن أمر بخلعها لينال بركة الوادي المقدس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers that removing the sandals taught humility before the gravity of the occasion, like the custom at royal courts; their material is irrelevant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r5.anchor: وتحتمل الآية معنى آخر هو الأليق بها عندي، وذلك أن الله تعالى أمره أن يتواضع لعظم الحال التي حصل فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r7.claim: طوى is explained as twice or doubled; groups also interpret it as sanctified twice, as Moses having traversed it, or as the name of the valley.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r7.anchor: معناه مرتين مرتين، فقالت فرقة معناه قدس مرتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r8.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r8.claim: These readers pronounce طوى with tanwin as a place name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «طوى» بالتنوين على أنه اسم المكان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r9.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r9.claim: These readers pronounce طوى without tanwin as a feminine place name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r9.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو «طوى» على أنه اسم البقعة دون تنوين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r10.speaker: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r10.claim: Abu Zayd reports from Abu ʿAmr a kasra on the ṭāʾ; another group reads طاوي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r10.anchor: وقرأ هؤلاء كلهم بضم الطاء، وقرأ أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو بكسر الطاء، وقرأت فرقة «طاوي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r11.claim: On the first interpretation, طوى is like ثنى: doubled or folded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r11.anchor: و «طوى» على التأويل الأول بمنزلة قولهم ثنى وثنى أي مثنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r17.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r17.claim: One group reads the phrase بالواد المقدس طاوي.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r1.claim: Repeating the pronoun strengthens the indication, confirms recognition, and removes doubt; the author compares 15:89.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r1.anchor: إني أنا ربك إنما كرر الكناية لتوكيد الدلالة وتحقيق المعرفة وإزالة الشبهة ومثله إني انا النذير المبين الحجر 89

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Abu Jaʿfar read anni with fatḥa on alif and yāʾ; most others read inni with kasra, while Nafiʿ has fatḥa on yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر أني بفتح الألف والياء وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي إني بكسر والألف إلا أن نافعا فتح الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says anni with fatḥa means “He called: I am your Lord”; inni with kasra means God addressed Moses, “I am your Lord.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج من قرأ أني انا بالفتح فالمعنى نودي بأني أنا ربك ومن قرا بالكسر فالمعنى نودي يا موسى فقال الله إني أنا ربك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud transmits from the Messenger of God that the sandals were made of the hide of a dead donkey; ʿAli and ʿIkrima also hold this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r4.anchor: أحدهما انهما كانا من جلد حمار ميت رواه ابن مسعود عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وبه قال علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه وعكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r5.claim: They say the sandals were from a slaughtered cow, and Moses was told to remove them to touch the sacred earth and receive its blessing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أنهما كانا من جلد بقرة ذكيت ولكنه أمر بخلعهما ليباشر تراب الأرض المقدسة فتناله بركتها قاله الحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r6.claim: The author says he has already discussed the two interpretations of the sacred valley under 5:21.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r6.anchor: فيه قولان قد ذكرناهما في المائدة 21 عند قوله الأرض المقدسة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and Abu ʿAmr read Ṭuwā without full declension; ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read it declinably.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو طوى وأنا غير مجراه وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي طوى مجراة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو حيوة وعلي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Haywa read Ṭuwā with kasra and tanwin; ʿAli ibn Nasr from Abu ʿAmr has kasra without tanwin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو حيوة طوى بكسر الطاء مع التنوين وقرأ علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو طوى بكسر الطاء من غير تنوين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats ḍamma forms with and without tanwin: the tanned form is a masculine valley name on faʿl; the untanned form may be a place name or an altered form like ʿUmar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج في طوى اربعة أوجه طوى بضم أوله من غير تنوين وبتنوين فمن نونه فهو اسم للوادي وهو مذكر سمي بمذكر على فعل نحو حطم وصرد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the untanned ḍamma form may be a place name, as in “the blessed spot,” or an altered form from ṭāwī, like ʿUmar from ʿĀmir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r10.anchor: ومن لم ينونه ترك صرفه من جهتين احداهما أن يكون معدولا عن طاو فيصير مثل عمر المعدول عن عامر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r11.claim: With kasra and tanwin, Ṭuwan resembles maʿan and means sanctified repeatedly; the cited line by ʿAdi ibn Zayd uses ṭuwan for repeated blame.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r11.anchor: وإذا كسر ونون فهو مثل معى والمعنى المقدس مرة بعد مرة كما قال عدي بن زيد أعاذل إن اللوم في غير كنهه علي طوى من غيك المتردد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r12.claim: The kasra form without tanwin is treated as a place name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p273#2/r12.anchor: ومن لم ينون جعله اسما للبقعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r1.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r1.claim: One reported interpretation makes Ṭuwā the proper name of the valley.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه اسم الوادي رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r2.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r2.claim: A second interpretation takes Ṭuwā to mean “tread on the valley”; Mujahid is also said to hold both this and the proper-name interpretation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r2.anchor: والثاني أن معنى طوى طأ الوادي رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس وعن مجاهد كالقولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say Ṭuwā means sanctified.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p274/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه قدس قاله الحسن وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.claim: God identifies Himself as the one speaking and addressing Moses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r3.anchor: وقال هاهنا {إني أنا ربك} أي: الذي يكلمك ويخاطبك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، أبو ذر، أبو أيوب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r4.claim: Ali, Abu Dharr, Abu Ayyub and other early authorities say Moses’ sandals were made from hide of a donkey that had not been ritually slaughtered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r4.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب، وأبو ذر، وأبو أيوب، وغير واحد من السلف: كانتا من جلد حمار غير ذكي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.claim: One explanation is that God commanded Moses to remove his sandals to show reverence for the sacred place; Saeed ibn Jubayr compares this to a man removing his sandals when entering the Kaaba.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كما يؤمر الرجل أن يخلع نعليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that Moses was to tread the sacred ground barefoot.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: ليطأ الأرض المقدسة بقدميه حافيا غير منتعل. وقيل: غير ذلك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Tuwa is the name of the valley; other authorities agree, and Ibn Kathir prefers this explanation, treating the word as an appositional clarification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r7.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: هو اسم للوادي. وكذا قال غير واحد، فعلى هذا يكون عطف بيان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.claim: Other suggestions take Tuwa as an order to tread the ground with the feet, or as indicating that the place was sanctified twice and its blessing doubled; Ibn Kathir rejects these in favor of the valley’s name.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p276#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: عبارة عن الأمر بالوطء بقدميه. وقيل: لأنه قدس مرتين، وطوى له البركة وكررت: والأول أصح،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.claim: Repeating the pronoun strengthens the proof, secures recognition, and removes doubt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.anchor: تكرير الضمير في { إني أنا ربك } لتوكيد الدلالة وتحقيق المعرفة وإماطة الشبهة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.claim: When Moses heard the call, he asked who was speaking; God replied, I am your Lord, but Satan then suggested that it might be a devil's voice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.anchor: روي أنه لما نودي { حديث موسى } قال : من المتكلم ؟ فقال له الله عز وجل : { إني أنا ربك }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.claim: Moses recognized God's voice because he heard it from all six directions and with all his limbs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.anchor: فقال : أنا عرفت أنه كلام الله بأني أسمعه من جميع جهاتي الست ، وأسمعه بجميع أعضائي .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.claim: Moses saw a green tree like bright white fire, heard the angels glorify God, and saw a great light; he was frightened, then calmed, and the tree was a buckthorn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.anchor: وروي : أنه حين انتهى رأى شجرة خضراء ، من أسفلها إلى أعلاها كأنها نار بيضاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.claim: Another report says the sound did not change when Moses moved nearer or farther away.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.anchor: وروي : كلما دنا أو بعد لم يختلف ما كان يسمع من الصوت .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the tree withdrew as Moses approached, then came nearer when he turned back, after which God spoke to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.anchor: وعن ابن إسحاق : لما دنا استأخرت عنه ، فلما رأى ذلك رجع وأوجس في نفسه خيفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.speaker: السدي وقتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi and Qatada say Moses had to remove sandals made of untanned hide from a dead donkey.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.anchor: قيل : أمر بخلع النعلين لأنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت غير مدبوغ عن السدي وقتادة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.claim: Another explanation is that Moses was to touch the valley barefoot for its blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : ليباشر الوادي بقدميه متبركا به .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.claim: Bare feet signify humility before God; reports say early Muslims circumambulated barefoot, and some treated entering a mosque in shoes as grave enough to merit charity if accidental.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : لأن الحفوة تواضع لله ، ومن ثم طاف السلف بالكعبة حافين ، ومنهم من استعظم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.claim: The Qur'an indicates that removing the sandals honored, magnified, and sanctified the place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.anchor: والقرآن يدل على أن ذلك احترام للبقعة وتعظيم لها وتشريف لقدسها .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.claim: A report says Moses removed his sandals and cast them behind the valley.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.anchor: وروي : أنه خلع نعليه وألقاهما من وراء الوادي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.claim: طوى is read with either ḍamma or kasra and may be declinable or indeclinable depending on whether it denotes a place or a region.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.anchor: { طوى } بالضم والكسر منصرف وغير منصرف بتأويل المكان والبقعة . وقيل : مرتين ، نحو ثنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r14.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r14.claim: Another explanation takes طوى as twice, suggesting two calls or that the valley was sanctified repeatedly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : مرتين ، نحو ثنى أي نودي نداءين أو قدس الوادي كرة بعد كرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، الحسن، ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r4.claim: Ali, al-Hasan, and Ibn Jurayj say Moses was told to remove his shoes so his feet would touch the holy valley's blessing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r4.anchor: ليباشر بقدميه بركة الوادي المقدس , قاله علي بن أبي طالب ، والحسن ، وابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r5.speaker: كعب، عكرمة، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r5.claim: Kaʿb, ʿIkrima, and Qatada say the shoes were made from the hide of a dead donkey.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r5.anchor: لأن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار ميت , قاله كعب , وعكرمة , وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid interpret المقدس as blessed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r6.anchor: أن المقدس هو المبارك , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas derives Ṭuwā from traversing the valley at night and thereby folding or crossing it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r8.anchor: أنه اسم من طوى لأنه مر بواديها ليلا فطواه , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r9.claim: A second explanation derives Ṭuwā from two calls: Arabic طوى can mean twice, as the second call overlays the first.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r9.anchor: سمي طوى لأن الله تعالى ناداه مرتين . وطوى في كلامهم بمعنى مرتين

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r10.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the valley was named Ṭuwā because it was sanctified twice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r10.anchor: بل سمي بذلك لأن الوادي قدس مرتين , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r11.claim: Mujahid interprets Ṭuwā as an instruction to tread the valley with one's foot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r11.anchor: أن معنى طوى : طإ الوادي بقدمك , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ṭuwā was the valley's ancient proper name.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r12.anchor: أنه الاسم للوادي قديما , قاله ابن زيد

MUJAHID:v1p394#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p394#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MUJAHID:v1p394#2/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains the command as telling Moses to tread barefoot, as one enters the Kaaba barefoot, out of reverence for the valley's blessing.
MUJAHID:v1p394#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله ﴿ طوى ﴾ قال يقول طأ الأرض حافيا كما تدخل الكعبة حافيا يعني من بركة الوادي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r1.claim: The hamza of innī is kasra because a call is a kind of speech and takes speech's treatment.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r1.anchor: بكسر الهمزة أي نودي فقيل يا موسى إني أولان النداء ضرب من القول فعومل معاملته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r2.claim: A report says Moses asked who spoke; God identified Himself, and Moses recognized God's speech because he heard from all six directions and with all his body.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r2.anchor: روى انها لما نودي يا موسى قال من المتكلم فقال الله عز وجل أنا ربك فعرف انه كلام الله عز وجل بأنه سمعه من جميع جهاته الست وسمعه بجميع أعضائه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r3.claim: Reasons offered: touch the blessed valley barefoot, sandals of untanned dead-donkey hide, or humility; the Quran indicates respect for the sacred place.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ فاخلع نعليك ﴾ انزعهما لتصيب قدميك بركة الوادي المقدس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r4.claim: The valley is purified or blessed.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r5.claim: Shāmī and Kufan readers except Ḥafṣ give Ṭuwā tanwīn as a proper valley name in apposition; others omit it as a place-name, while Abū Zayd has ṭāʾ with kasra and no tanwīn.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#5/r5.anchor: حيث كان منون شامي وكوفي لانه اسم علم للوادي وهو بدل منه وغيرهم بغير تنوين بتأويل البقعة وقرأ أبو زيد بكسر الطاء بلا تنوين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet describing Moses in wool clothes and sandals from a dead donkey's hide.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r9.anchor: روى الترمذي عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.speaker: الترمذي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report gharīb, known only through Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj; Qurṭubī identifies the Kūfan Ḥumayd ibn ʿAlī as munkar and Meccan Ḥumayd ibn Qays as trustworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r10.anchor: قال: هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من حديث حميد الأعرج حميد هو ابن علي الكوفي منكر الحديث،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.claim: The common reading has إني with kasra, treating it as the words said after Moses was called; Abū ʿUbayd chooses it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r11.anchor: وقرأ العامة «إني» بالكسر أي نودي فقيل له يا موسى إني، واختاره أبو عبيد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r12.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Ḥumayd read أني with fatḥa, governed by the call.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد «أني» بفتح الألف بإعمال النداء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r13.speaker: كعب وعكرمة وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r13.claim: Kaʿb, ʿIkrima, and Qatāda say Moses removed the sandals because they were impure, made from hide of an animal not ritually slaughtered.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r13.anchor: فقيل: أمر بطرح النعلين لأنها نجسة إذ هي من جلد غير مذكى قاله كعب وعكرمة وقتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والحسن وابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r14.claim: ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Jurayj say removal let Moses receive the valley's blessing and touch its soil with his feet.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r14.anchor: وقيل: أمر بذلك لينال بركة الوادي المقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r15.claim: Another explanation is that removing sandals showed humility while conversing with God.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r15.anchor: وقيل: أمر بخلع النعلين للخشوع والتواضع عند مناجاة الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r16.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r16.claim: A further view treats removal as honoring the sacred place, like entering the sanctuary barefoot.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r16.anchor: وقيل: إعظاما لذلك الموضع كما أن الحرم لا يدخل بنعلين إعظاما له

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r17.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Moses was told to tread barefoot, as people enter the Kaʿba barefoot.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r17.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: قيل له طإ الأرض حافيا كما تدخل الكعبة حافيا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r18.claim: Royal custom removes shoes to display utmost humility; on this explanation the sandals' material is irrelevant.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r18.anchor: والعرف عند الملوك أن تخلع النعال ويبلغ الإنسان إلى غاية التواضع

QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r19.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r19.claim: Mālik would not ride an animal in Madina, out of reverence for soil containing honored bones and the Prophet's noble body.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:11-12/r19.anchor: وقد كان مالك لا يرى لنفسه ركوب دابة بالمدينة برا بتربتها المحتوية على الأعظم الشريفة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r1.claim: Untanned dead-animal leather is impure by agreement except according to al-Zuhrī and al-Layth; purification was discussed under Sūrat Barāʾa.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r1.anchor: فأما لو كانت النعل والخف من جلد ميتة فإن كان غير مدبوغ فهو نجس باتفاق، ما عدا ما ذهب إليه الزهري والليث،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r2.claim: Muqaddas means purified; quds is purity, and holy land is so named because God removed disbelievers and settled believers there.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r2.anchor: المقدس: المطهر. والقدس: الطهارة، والأرض المقدسة أي المطهرة سميت بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r3.claim: God may favor places, times, and creatures; the valley's sanctity cannot rest only on expelling disbelievers and settling believers, since other places share that trait.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r3.anchor: ولله أن يفضل ما شاء. وعلى هذا فلا اعتبار بكونه مقدسا بإخراج الكافرين وإسكان المؤمنين فقد شاركه في ذلك غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and others identify Ṭuwā as the valley's name.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r4.anchor: و«طوى» اسم الوادي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it is a deep, rounded valley, like a well.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو واد عميق مستدير مثل الطوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r6.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r6.claim: Qurṭubī records a form attributed to ʿIkrima and another for the other readers; this excerpt prints them identically.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r7.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r7.claim: Al-Jawharī says Ṭuwā is a Syrian place name; ṭāʾ may take kasra or ḍamma, and the name may be declinable or indeclinable.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r7.anchor: قال الجوهري: «طوى» اسم موضع بالشام، تكسر طاؤه وتضم، ويصرف ولا يصرف،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r8.claim: Some connect Ṭuwā with a doubled or folded thing, interpreting the valley as sanctified twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: «طوى» مثل «طوى» وهو الشيء المثني، وقالوا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says blessing and sanctification were doubled in the valley.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: ثنيت فيه البركة والتقديس مرتين.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r10.claim: According to Ibn ʿAbbās as quoted by al-Mahdawī, Moses traversed the valley by night and ascended it; Ṭuwā is a verbal noun for passing through it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r10.anchor: وذكر المهدوي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أنه قيل له «طوى» لأن موسى طواه بالليل إذ مر به

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r11.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan also treats Ṭuwā as a verbal noun meaning sanctified twice.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r11.anchor: الحسن: معناه أنه قدس مرتين فهو مصدر من طويته طوى أيضا.

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.claim: In the inward reading, light signifies love and fire signifies ardent love; when Moses' love and longing were full, the essential light appeared in the form of attribute-fire, burned away his selfhood, and brought single-hearted orientation.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r6.anchor: يقول الفقير : النور للمحبة والنار للعشق

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r7.claim: The repeated pronouns stress certainty: Moses is told to have no doubt that the speaker is his Lord.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r7.anchor: للتوكيد والتحقق يعني (شك مكن ومتيقن شوكه من)

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r8.claim: Removing the sandals is commanded because going barefoot better expresses humility and proper decorum before God.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r8.anchor: أمر بذلك لأن الحفوة أدخل في التواضع وحسن الأدب

BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r9.claim: Bishr al-Hafi and other pious predecessors walked barefoot, and earlier generations circumambulated the Kaaba barefoot.
BURSEVI:v5p284#2/r9.anchor: ولذلك كان بشر الحافي ونحوه يسيرون حفاة وكان السلف الصالحون يطوفون بالكعبة حافين

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r1.claim: One explanation says Moses' bare feet honor the holy valley by his arrival and connect its blessing to him.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r1.anchor: ليتشرف مشهد الوادي بقدوم قدميه وتتصل بركة الأرض إليه

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r2.claim: Another says the Beloved was told to approach the Throne's carpet in sandals so the Throne would be honored by their dust and its light would reach him; this applies to Muhammad's rank, unlike Moses' station.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r2.anchor: وقيل للحبيب تقدم على بساط العرش بنعليك ليتشرف العرش بغبار نعال قدميك

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r3.claim: A report about Abū Ḥanīfa says that when he visited the caliph, the caliph asked him to stay mounted and tread on the caliph's carpet with his mule.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r3.anchor: وذكر في فضائل أبي حنيفة أنه كان إذا قدم على الخليفة للزيارة

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r4.speaker: حل الرموز
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r4.claim: One explanation says the sandals were made of untanned donkey hide, making the command a matter of decorum.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r4.anchor: أو لأنهما كانا غير مدبوغين من جلد الحمار فالخطاب خطاب التأديب كما في "حل الرموز"

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r5.claim: Kāshifī considers it more correct that the sandals were made of processed, ritually pure cowhide.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (أصح آنست كه نعلين از جلد بقربود وطاهر)

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r6.speaker: الأسرار المحمدية
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r6.claim: A dream interpretation takes the sandals to mean a man's wife; another commentary glosses removing them as setting aside concern for wife and sheep.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r6.anchor: قال في "الأسرار المحمدية" جاء في غرائب التفسير في قوله سبحانه

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r7.speaker: الشيخ افتاده
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r7.claim: Sheikh Aftade interprets the sandals as nature and the self; Bursevī agrees that wife represents nature, child the self, and sheep livelihood, so Moses is told to leave all such concerns behind.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r7.anchor: وقال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بافتاده قدس سره يعني الطبيعة والنفس

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r8.claim: Some say the two sandals signify this world and the next, so Moses is ordered to become wholly absorbed in knowing and beholding God.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : "المراد بالنعلين الدنيا والآخرة كأنه أمره بالاستغراق

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r9.claim: Others take the sandals as the two premises proving a Creator: once one reaches knowledge of God, one should stop attending to the proof and remain absorbed in sacred light.
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن إثبات الصانع يكون بمقدمتين فشبهتا بالنعلين إذ بهما يتوصل

BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r10.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p284#3/r10.claim: Rūmī's cited verse begins an analogy about reaching the roof of heaven, which makes the search for a ladder unnecessary.

BURSEVI:v5p285/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r1.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v5p285/r1.claim: Rūmī says that once the clear mirror of realization is polished, polishing it further is ignorance, just as seeking a messenger's letter is ugly before a welcoming king.
BURSEVI:v5p285/r1.anchor: آينه روشن كه شد صاف وجلى

BURSEVI:v5p285/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r2.speaker: الشبلي
BURSEVI:v5p285/r2.claim: After reaching God, al-Shiblī washed all his books, illustrating that discursive proofs are left behind after realization.
BURSEVI:v5p285/r2.anchor: غسل حضرة الشيخ الشبلي قدس سره جميع كتبه بعد الوصول إلى الله

BURSEVI:v5p285/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r3.claim: The sanctified valley is pure and set apart from evil.
BURSEVI:v5p285/r3.anchor: {إنك بالواد المقدس} المطهر والمتبعد من السوء

BURSEVI:v5p285/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r4.claim: Tuwa is an appositive proper name for the valley; with tanwin it is declined as a place name, while without it it is indeclinable as a known region.

BURSEVI:v5p285/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r5.claim: A report says Moses removed his sandals and cast them beyond the valley.
BURSEVI:v5p285/r5.anchor: روي أن موسى عليه السلام خلعهما وألقاهما وراء الوادي

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r1.speaker: قالوا
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r1.claim: The repeated pronoun in إني أنا ربك is said to strengthen the indication and remove doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r1.anchor: قالوا : إن تكرير الضمير في { إنى أنا ربك } كان لتوليد الدلالة وإزالة الشبهة

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r2.speaker: علي ومقاتل والكلبي والضحاك وقتادة والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r2.claim: ʿAlī, Muqātil, al-Kalbī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatāda, and al-Suddī say Moses’ sandals were made from carrion donkey hide, so he had to remove them to protect the holy valley.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r2.anchor: وهذا قول علي عليه السلام وقول مقاتل والكلبي والضحاك وقتادة والسدي

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Mujāhid say the sandals were removed so Moses’ feet could receive the valley’s blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r3.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r4.claim: The command may express reverence for the holy place: Moses should approach barefoot, humbly and in awe while hearing God’s speech; the next clause explains why.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r4.anchor: أن يحمل ذلك على تعظيم البقعة من أن يطأها إلا حافيا ليكون معظما لها وخاضعا عند سماع كلام ربه

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r5.claim: An inward reading takes sandals in dreams to signify wife and child: Moses is told not to let concern for them occupy his heart.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r5.anchor: أن النعل في النوم يفسر بالزوجة والولد

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r6.claim: Another inward reading makes the sandals attachment to both this world and the next; Moses should be wholly absorbed in knowing God, the holy valley signifying divine purity.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r6.anchor: المراد بخلع النعلين ترك الالتفات إلى الدنيا والآخرة كأنه أمره بأن يصير مستغرق القلب بالكلية في معرفة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r7.claim: A third reading likens the two sandals to premises used to infer the Creator: after reaching divine knowledge, one should cease attending to the premises and become absorbed in God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p15#2/r7.anchor: هاتان المقدمتان تشبهان النعلين لأن بهما يتوصل العقل إلى المقصود ويتنقل من النظر في الخلق إلى معرفة الخالق

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r1.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that if God’s speech were eternal, He would have commanded Moses before his existence, like absurdly addressing absent people in an empty house.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r1.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بقوله : { فاخلع نعليك } على أن كلام الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r2.claim: The first reply is that God’s speech is eternal, but it was not an imperative or prohibition in eternity.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r2.anchor: أن كلامه تعالى وإن كان قديما إلا أنه في الأزل لم يكن أمرا ولا نهيا

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r3.claim: The second reply treats the eternal speech as an order whose persistence makes the person commanded in the future without any change in that speech, analogously to eternal power yielding capacity for action later.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r3.anchor: أنه كان أمرا بمعنى أنه وجد في الأزل شيء لما استمر إلى ما لا يزال صار الشخص به مأمورا من غير وقوع التغير في ذلك الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r4.claim: The verse does not establish that praying or circumambulating in sandals is disliked: if removal honored the valley, that command was specific to the occasion.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r4.anchor: ليس في الآية دلالة على كراهة الصلاة والطواف في النعل والصحيح عدم الكراهة وذلك لأنا إن عللنا الأمر بخلع النعلين بتعظيم الوادي

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r5.claim: The Prophet says that any hide tanned becomes pure; if the sandals’ leather was forbidden carrion donkey hide, that earlier prohibition would be abrogated by this ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r5.anchor: فإن كان كذلك فهو منسوخ بقوله عليه السلام : ( أيما إيهاب دبغ فقد طهر )

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r6.claim: The Prophet prayed in sandals, then removed them after Gabriel told him they were soiled; he asked why others had removed theirs, showing he did not disapprove of footwear itself.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r6.anchor: وقد صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في نعليه ثم خلعهما في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r7.claim: طوى is read with ḍamma or kasra, with or without tanwīn.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r7.anchor: قرىء طوى بالضم والكسر منصرفا وغير منصرف

RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r8.claim: With tanwīn طوى is the valley’s name; without it, it is treated as a diptote derived from طاوي, like ʿUmar from ʿĀmir.
RAZI-FULL:v22p16/r8.anchor: فمن نونه فهو اسم الوادي ومن لم ينونه ترك صرفه لأنه معدول عن طاوي فهو مثل عمر المعدول عن عامر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r6.speaker: خلف عن الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r6.claim: Khalaf claims al-Kisāʾī preferred stopping with yāʾ on الواد; Ibn Mujāhid rejects this because it is written without yāʾ for connected recitation.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r6.anchor: وزعم خلف عن الكسائى أنه كان يستحب أن يقف عليها بالياء ولا ينبغى أن يوقف عليها لأنها كتبت بغير ياء على الوصل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r9.claim: Removing the sandals symbolizes turning away from worldly and otherworldly concerns, letting the heart be wholly absorbed in knowing God and attending to nothing else.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r9.anchor: فاخلع نعليكاترك الالتفات إلى الدنيا والاخرة وسر مستغرق القلب بالكلية فى معرفة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r10.claim: Another interpretation makes the sandals the two premises of a proof; Moses is told to leave inference behind because he is in the valley of direct knowledge of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : النعلان إشارة إلى المقدمتين اللتين يتركب منهما الدليل لانهما يتوصل بهما العقل إلى المقصود

ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r11.claim: The sacred valley Ṭuwā is the valley of God's holy majesty and the transcendence of His might.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p209#2/r11.anchor: انك بالوادى المقدس طوى وهو وادى قدس جلال الله تعالى وتنزه عزته عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r6.claim: Removing sandals signifies emptying the conscience of distractions; what follows signifies adorning it and acquiring what was absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى التخلية وتطهير لوح الضمير من الاغيار وما بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r9.claim: Feet enable escape and hands pursuit; surrendering sandals and staff teaches that self-directed seeking and fleeing impede complete absorption in gnosis, even for a great prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r9.anchor: موسى عليه السلام كان في رجله شئ وهو النعل وفى يده شئ وهو العصا وارجل الة الهرب واليد الة الطلب

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r5.claim: The holy valley is the purified place where God manifested Himself to Moses, spoke to him, and entrusted him with his mission.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r5.anchor: والوادي المقدس، هو المكمان المطهر الذي تجلى فيه سبحانه لموسى وكلمه، وألقى إليه رسالته

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r6.claim: One reported reading has Ṭuwā with ḍamma, a shortened form, and tanwīn.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r6.anchor: قرئت: طُوًى، بالضم والقصر والتنوين، وقيل هي علم على الوادي المقدس

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r7.speaker: قيل
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r7.claim: A reported view treats Ṭuwā as the valley's proper name and parses it as apposition or explicative apposition.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r7.anchor: وقيل هي علم على الوادي المقدس، فتعرب بدلاً أو عطف بيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r7.claim: Moses recognized a divine address because unusual created sounds came from no visible person or angelic intermediary; they signified God’s intent, the inner speech subsisting in God beyond letters, sounds, or hearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p195/r7.anchor: والمراد التي تدل عليه تلك الأصوات الخارقة للعادة هو ما نسميه بالكلام النفسي . وليس الكلام النفسي هو الذي سمعه موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r1.claim: Calling himself Moses’ Lord calms his fear of an unseen speaker, since a lord is gentle toward the one under his care.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r1.anchor: والإخبار عن ضمير المتكلم بأنه رب المخاطب لتسكين روعة نفسه من خطاب لا يرى مخاطبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r2.claim: Inna confirms the surprising message and prevents Moses from doubting the source of the speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بحرف ( إن ) لتحقيقه لأجل غرابته دفعا لتطرق الشك عن موسى في مصدر هذا الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read annī with fatḥa on the hamza, taking an omitted preposition: “he was called that I am your Lord”; emphasis remains in either reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير ( أني ) بفتح الهمزة على حذف باء الجر . والتقدير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r4.claim: The command to remove the sandals follows the declaration of lordship to signal that the place became sacred through divine speech occurring there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r4.anchor: وتفريع الأمر بخلع النعلين على الإعلام بأنه ربه إشارة إلى أن ذلك المكان قد حله التقديس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r5.claim: Khalaʿ means separating something attached; sandals are thick leather foot coverings tied with leather straps to protect against ground and stones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r5.anchor: والخلع : فصل شيء عن شيء كان متصلا به . والنعلان : جلدان غليظان يجعلان تحت الرجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r6.claim: God ordered Moses to remove his sandals to honor the place where he would hear divine speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r6.anchor: وإنما أمره الله بخلع نعليه تعظيما منه لذلك المكان الذي سيسمع فيه الكلام الإلهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r7.claim: Al-Tirmidhī transmits from Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet, that Moses’ sandals were made of the hide of a dead donkey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r7.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( كانت نعلاه من جلد حمار ميت )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r8.claim: The command also conveys humility, but this circumstance does not establish a general requirement to remove sandals during prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r8.anchor: أقول : وفيه أيضا زيادة خشوع . وقد اقتضى كلا المعنيين قوله تعالى : { إنك بالواد المقدس }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r9.claim: Wād is a pass between mountains or hills, originally ending in yāʾ; the yāʾ is often dropped but retained in the dual and annexation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r9.anchor: والواد : المفرج بين الجبال والتلالل . وأصله بياء في آخره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r10.claim: Muqaddas means purified and sanctified; places become sacred through honored events occurring there, here the divine address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r10.anchor: والمقدس : المطهر المنزه . وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { ونقدس لك في أول البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r11.claim: Ṭuwā has been read with either ḍamma or kasra, though the well-known reading has only ḍamma.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r11.anchor: وهو بضم الطاء وبكسرها ، ولم يقرأ في المشهور إلا بضم الطاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r12.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r12.claim: One view takes Ṭuwā as the proper name of the valley.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r13.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r13.claim: Another view treats Ṭuwā as a verbal noun in the passive sense: the valley Moses traversed that night.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r13.anchor: وقيل : هو اسم مصدر مثل هدى ، وصف بالمصدر بمعنى اسم المفعول ، أي طواه موسى بالسير في تلك الليلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r14.claim: Within the verbal-noun reading, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers an imperative for Moses to traverse the valley and climb to its upper end for revelation; another report says Moses climbed there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r14.anchor: وأحسن منه على هذا الوجه أن يقال هو أمر لموسى بأن يطوي الوادي ويصعد إلى أعلاه لتلقي الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r15.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r15.claim: A further view derives Ṭuwā from folding and takes it to mean sanctified twice, an intensified sanctification; compare the doubled sense in 67:4.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p196/r15.anchor: وقيل : هو بمعنى المقدس تقديسين ، لأن الطي هو جعل الثوب على شقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr takes Ṭuwā as a kind of valley, narrow like folded cloth or deep like a lined well; a valley outside Mecca was called Dhū Ṭuwā, where arriving pilgrims are recommended to bathe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r1.anchor: اسم لصنف من الأودية يكون ضيقا بمنزلة الثوب المطوي أو غائرا كالبئر المطوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r2.claim: He notes disagreement over whether Ṭuwā is declinable: it may be indeclinable as a foreign name or because it is altered from Ṭāw, as ʿUmar from ʿĀmir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r2.anchor: هل ينصرف أو يمنع من الصرف بناء على أنه اسم أعجمي أو لأنه معدول عن طاو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r3.claim: The majority read Ṭuwā without tanwīn, treating it as diptote.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r3.anchor: بلا تنوين على منعه من الصرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read it with tanwīn because it is a masculine valley name.

RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r3.claim: The sandals signify flight and the staff pursuit: first removing the sandals, then casting the staff, symbolizes abandoning both escape and seeking to become wholly devoted to God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r3.anchor: الرجل آلة الهرب واليد آلة الطلب فقال أولا : { فاخلع نعليك }

RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r4.claim: Even eminent Moses had to put aside his only two possessions, sandals and staff, before approaching God; a sinner burdened with a thousand loads of sin should consider how to approach.
RAZI-FULL:v22p24/r4.anchor: لما وصل إلى الحضرة ولم يكن معه إلا النعلان والعصا أمره بالقائهما حتى أمكنه الوصول
